item.title: Brasileños eligen entre Lula y Flávio Bolsonaro en balotaje presidencial
item.description: Los brasileños votaban el domingo en una reñida segunda vuelta electoral que podría inclinar bruscamente a la derecha a la nación más grande de América Latina, acercándola a Estados Unidos como parte de un giro conservador más amplio en toda la región.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin
item.content:encoded: Los brasileños votaban el domingo en una reñida segunda vuelta electoral que podría inclinar bruscamente a la derecha a la nación más grande de América Latina, acercándola a Estados Unidos como parte de un giro conservador más amplio en toda la región. La segunda vuelta enfrenta al presidente izquierdista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva con el senador derechista Flávio Bolsonaro. El hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro dio la sorpresa a principios de mes al liderar la votación en la primera vuelta en contra de lo que decían las encuestas. Un triunfo de Bolsonaro, de 45 años, prolongaría la ola de victorias de la derecha para los candidatos latinoamericanos afines a Donald Trump, mientras que un cuarto mandato para Lula sería una decepción en Washington, que ha tenido roces con su gobierno en materia de comercio y seguridad. Reuters reveló el sábado una campaña dentro del Departamento de Estado de Trump para ayudar a que los Bolsonaro volvieran al poder. La contienda electoral ha estado marcada por escándalos de corrupción, incertidumbre económica y acusaciones de injerencia estadounidense, algo que Washington niega. También se ha visto influenciada por las repercusiones de la condena de Jair Bolsonaro en 2025 por planear un golpe de Estado en 2022, ante la promesa de Flávio de liberar a su padre si resulta elegido. Trump calificó el caso de "caza de brujas" e impuso un arancel del 50% a Brasil en 2025, en una decisión vinculada explícitamente al juicio de Jair Bolsonaro. Si bien muchas de estas medidas fueron posteriormente suavizadas, el mandatario republicano impuso nuevos aranceles a Brasil este año, alegando prácticas comerciales desleales. Lula ha presentado la cercanía del Gobierno de Trump con el clan Bolsonaro como parte de un intento de influir en las elecciones, al tiempo que ha calificado los aranceles y otras medidas punitivas de intimidación. En materia económica, a pesar de la disminución de la desigualdad y el desempleo, Lula ha tenido dificultades para ganarse a un electorado que lidia con el alto costo de la vida y las elevadas deudas familiares. La violencia endémica de las pandillas también preocupa a los votantes. Bolsonaro ha intentado sacar provecho de la preocupación por el costo de la vida y también ha prometido mano dura para combatir la delincuencia, comprometiéndose a construir cárceles de máxima seguridad y a aplicar la castración química para los delitos sexuales graves. Al emitir su voto en Río de Janeiro el domingo, Flávio Bolsonaro instó a la gente a acudir a las urnas "con lluvia o con sol". Lula, por su parte, votará en São Bernardo do Campo, cerca de São Paulo. RESULTADO INCIERTO Las encuestas muestran que los candidatos están prácticamente empatados de cara a la segunda vuelta, con recortando distancias en los últimos días. Sin embargo, los precedentes históricos favorecen a Bolsonaro, ya que ningún candidato ha ganado la presidencia tras quedar segundo en la primera vuelta de las elecciones. Bolsonaro obtuvo el 47% de los votos emitidos en la primera vuelta, contra e 45% de Lula. La victoria del senador disparó los mercados brasileños y su moneda ante las expectativas de reformas favorables a las empresas. Su éxito en la primera vuelta se vio reflejado en las elecciones al Congreso de su Partido Liberal y de otros políticos de derecha, lo que podría allanarle el camino legislativo o complicarle la gobernabilidad a Lula.

item.title: Conservative party wins first election in nearly a century in British Columbia
item.description: The opposition Conservative Party won an election in the Canadian province of British Columbia for the first time in nearly 100 years, promising to ramp up liquefied natural gas production, provisional results showed on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The opposition Conservative Party won an election in the Canadian province of British Columbia for the first time in nearly 100 years, promising to ramp up liquefied natural gas production, provisional results showed on Sunday. The result marks an end to nine years of power for the left-of-center New Democrats, who voiced opposition to new oil pipelines and supported a ban on tankers along the province's northern coast The right-leaning Conservatives won 64 of the 93 seats and the New Democrats won 27. It is the first Conservative provincial election win since 1928 The Conservatives pledged to double natural gas production by 2032 and more than triple it by 2035 "I believe in energy... We will cut red tape like it's never been cut before," Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson said in his victory speech Doerkson, who will become the next premier of the province, promised to "supercharge" BC. The province will host a business summit in Vancouver next year The Conservatives promised to end emissions limits, replace the province's carbon tax framework and reach out to energy providers that had left the province's LNG sector since 2018, including ExxonMobil, Chevron and Woodside Polls showed voters were focused on cost-of-living issues, healthcare, and the ongoing trade war with US President Donald Trump New Democrat Premier David Eby had called for a strong mandate to confront Trump's tariff threats

item.title: Netanyahu rebuked for plan to use crypto to bypass economic sanctions
item.description: His comments drew a rare rebuke by the Bank of Israel.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces [USN:L8N45Y0MD TEXT:"re-election"] this week, is drawing criticism from economists and political rivals after suggesting Israel could use cryptocurrency to help shield its economy from potential international sanctions. In an interview with Israel's Channel 10 on Friday, Netanyahu said he was preparing for a scenario in which broader sanctions were imposed on Israel. Last month, Britain, France and Canada said they would [USN:S8N42N05Y TEXT:"block imports"] from Israeli settlements in the West Bank in what was the latest in a series of actions targeting Israel's settlement policy, underscoring its growing diplomatic isolation among some of its traditional allies. "There could be sanctions, and sanctions on banks so you need to set up a bypass economy," Netanyahu said. "You know, there are currencies that can bypass (sanctions). We are also working on that." Asked whether he was referring to cryptocurrency, Netanyahu replied: "Very true, very true," adding that blockchain technology was another possibility. The comments drew a rare rebuke by the Bank of Israel, which said crypto currencies cannot serve as a route to bypass sanctions and that political leaders should focus on policy that would render such measures unnecessary. "The right course for Israel's economy is to preserve our economic relations with our main trading partners, and to focus on preventing sanctions and their negative impact on the economy," it said. Netanyahu on Sunday continued to defend his record, urging voters to back him and saying he and US President Donald Trump had two years left to work together to topple Iran's rulers . PLAN DRAWS CRITICISM On Sunday, more than 100 economists, including former Bank of Israel officials, ex-central bank governor Jacob Frenkel and several Nobel laureates, signed a letter expressing alarm over Netanyahu's proposal. They said it would lead to higher unemployment, a fall in foreign investment and the collapse of Israel's economic standing in the world. "As we have seen in countries that have suffered similar sanctions, such as South Africa, Iran, and Russia, the living standards of Israeli citizens would plummet dramatically, and the state's ability to finance its security and defend itself against its enemies would be severely damaged," the letter read. "Netanyahu is knowingly leading the State of Israel toward boycott and international economic isolation, and all he has to offer the Israeli economy is a puzzling solution, one accepted in criminal organizations, that will not help in the slightest." Netanyahu's main rival in Tuesday's election, [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Gadi Eisenkot"], called the crypto plan "madness" and said he feared that the "BibiCoin policy" would drive companies abroad and undermine national security. Opposition leader Yair Lapid said: "Netanyahu has gone off the rails ... He promises the citizens of Israel before these elections that they'll be standing in line for an hour and a half for bread, like in Russia and Iran." Opinion polls point to a potential stalemate in the election with neither Netanyahu's ruling coalition nor an opposition alliance securing a governing majority in parliament.

item.title: British pin hopes of late SailGP lift on training blitz
item.description: Britain have struggled off the start line this season but the defending champions were the first to grab a week of intensive training at SailGP's new performance facility as they pursue a Grand Final berth, skipper Dylan Fletcher said.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Smith
item.content:encoded: Britain have struggled off the start line this season but the defending champions were the first to grab a week of intensive training at SailGP's new performance facility as they pursue a Grand Final berth, skipper Dylan Fletcher said. With only two events left, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi next month, the British are fifth in the championship, just behind the US and Sweden, in pursuit of a top-three finish that would earn a place in the winner-takes-all Grand Final. "We put our name down early to get one of these slots and I think that it's a really good opportunity," Fletcher told Reuters at the start of a week practising in Pensacola, Florida. SailGP gives crews very little practice on board their F50 catamarans, which can hit more than 100 kph when they lift above the water on foils, a gap the new facility aims to bridge. "We haven't had the season that we've been happy with at the moment. And this in reality feels like a great opportunity, not just on the water, but off the water," said Fletcher, ahead of the team's first 2-1/2-hour F50 session. "We're mainly focused on light wind starting... We've seen that as much as we've been still quite good at overtaking, the reality is it's all about the start," said Fletcher. "The Aussies have been the standout performers and you know that shows," he added of how the season's leaders start. The British are seeking short-term gains with their week in Pensacola, which can offer the lighter wind conditions that are the norm in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, as well as looking ahead to next season, which starts in Hong Kong in January. "We want to try and finish this season strong regardless of how it goes... to start off on the right foot (next season) because we obviously haven't been sailing at the level that we expect," Fletcher said. Despite the team's dip in form, Fletcher has not given up. "If we sail well enough to win the Grand Final, then we will be in the Grand Final. The momentum is almost more important going into those last two events," the 38-year-old said. "If you look at how the results generally go, I'd say if we made the final in both (Dubai and Abu Dhabi), it would be surprising if we weren't in the Grand Final," he added. While Spain's Los Gallos have "pretty much qualified", they have "everything to lose", Fletcher said, adding that the "British underdogs" had "absolutely nothing to lose". The British are focusing particularly on the pre-start "trigger" manoeuvre used to make sure the boat hits the line at top speed, along with Fletcher's positioning on the course. "We're going to try and execute that and have a bit of a change in our strategy," Fletcher said, adding: "Hopefully we can just tip the scales back in our favour, and we'll be away and looking like the team that we know we can be."

item.title: Rybakina brushes aside Fernandez to retain Ningbo crown
item.description: Elena Rybakina blazed past unseeded Canadian Leylah Fernandez 6-2 6-2 to retain her Ningbo Open title and lift her first trophy as the world number one ahead of the WTA Finals next month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elena Rybakina blazed past unseeded Canadian Leylah Fernandez 6-2 6-2 in the Ningbo Open final on Sunday to retain her title and lift her first trophy as the world number one ahead of the WTA Finals next month. The victory in Ningbo also helped the Kazakh to take a big step towards securing the year-end number one ranking, further burnishing a spectacular season in which she won the Australian Open title before adding the US Open crown to reach the summit. "It's amazing to play in front of you... it's my second year here and my second win," Rybakina told the crowd in the eastern Chinese city after collecting a tour-leading fourth title of the season and 15th overall. "It's such a special place for me. Thanks so much Ningbo." Rybakina's latest triumph is a timely lift after setbacks in Beijing and Wuhan, as she turns her attention to the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo this week before she launches her title defence at the season finale in Indian Wells, California, from November 8. TRADEMARK POWER Top seed Rybakina made the breakthrough with her trademark power in the fifth game and then unleashed a searing crosscourt backhand winner to go 4-2 up, before the 27-year-old wrapped up the opening set in 38 minutes. World number 30 Fernandez made a bright start to the next set but Rybakina absorbed the pressure and raised her level to force an error and break for 2-1, with the three-times Grand Slam champion breezing to victory from there. Fernandez, who won the Singapore Open last month, remained upbeat despite a disappointing showing in the final and backed herself to finish the season strongly after a gruelling run of matches in Ningbo. "I'd like to congratulate Elena for a wonderful week and a wonderful year. Congratulations to you and your team," the 24-year-old said, before addressing her own team. "We're having a good end of year. We've just got to keep going and keep working hard."

item.title: Serbia election: Main players, voter concerns and what is at stake
item.description: Serbia is holding parliamentary elections on Sunday, in which a popular student movement is seeking to end the rule of longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic.
item.dc:creator: Canan Sevgili, Arda Dipova, Ivana Sekularac
item.content:encoded: Serbia is holding [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"parliamentary elections"] on Sunday, in which a popular student movement is seeking to end the rule of longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic. Here are the main players, issues and stakes in the vote. WHO ARE THE MAJOR PLAYERS AND WHAT DO THEY STAND FOR? Aleksandar Vucic – United Serbia: The Serbian Progressive Party (SNS)-led electoral list is campaigning on economic growth, higher wages and pensions, infrastructure investment and political stability. SNS leader Milos Vucevic has pledged 4% economic growth in 2027. Vucic, who resigned as president on September 27, is running to become prime minister. Students Win: Emerging from protests over the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse that killed 16 people, the anti-corruption movement has campaigned for accountability and transparent public procurement. The Democratic Party and Kreni Promeni movement have backed it rather than fielding their own lists. Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) – Ivica Dacic – Factor of Stability: A longstanding ally of the SNS, the pro-Russian SPS leads a coalition with Unified Serbia, the Social Democratic Party of Serbia and the Greens of Serbia. It campaigns on social justice, workers' rights and welfare, political stability, and national interests. European Serbia: A pro-European opposition alliance led by Marinika Tepic and Zdravko Ponos, bringing together the Party of Freedom and Justice, Serbia Centre, and the Solidarity, Self-Defence and Liberation movement. It advocates closer European integration, sanctions against Russia and democratic reforms. WHAT ARE PARTY LISTS AND HOW DO THEY WORK? Political parties, party coalitions, movements and other groups can submit party lists, or electoral lists comprising no more than 250 candidates. The election commission has approved a total of 18 lists. On election day, voters vote for one electoral list on the ballot, rather than individual candidates. WHAT ARE THE MAIN ISSUES FOR VOTERS? Corruption and government accountability have dominated the campaign since the Novi Sad disaster. Protesters accuse Vucic and his allies of corruption, controlling the media and mistreating demonstrators, allegations the authorities deny. Living standards, economic development and the fairness of the electoral process are also campaign issues. HOW WILL A VICTORY OR LOSS FOR VUCIC IMPACT SERBIA AT HOME AND ABROAD? A victory allowing Vucic to become prime minister would extend his political leadership and could preserve Serbia's balancing act between its ambition to join the European Union and maintain Belgrade's close ties with Russia and China. A defeat could pave the way for sweeping domestic reforms, including stronger institutions and measures against corruption.

item.title: Flávio e Lula disputam Presidência em eleição que pode ser definida pela abstenção

item.dc:creator: Eduardo Simões
item.content:encoded: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) decidem neste domingo quem governará o Brasil a partir de 5 de janeiro de 2027 após uma das campanhas eleitorais mais tensas e recheadas de acusações da história da política brasileira, sem que as pesquisas apontem um favorito claro e com um provável papel decisivo do comparecimento dos eleitores às urnas. Senador de oposição e filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio, de 45 anos, largou na frente após um resultado surpreendente no primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, quando terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos, contra 45,16% de Lula. O atual presidente e candidato à reeleição, que completará 81 anos na próxima terça e que busca um quarto mandato presidencial, reduziu gradativamente a distância para o rival nas pesquisas de intenção de voto mais recentes, o que leva a corrida a um cenário incerto. “O que o povo fez comigo nesses dias é uma coisa que não tem como pagar, é muita generosidade, é muito carinho, é muito amor e eu serei eternamente grato ao comportamento do povo”, disse o petista a jornalistas após votar na manhã deste domingo, em São Bernardo do Campo (SP), berço político do Partido dos Trabalhadores. As [USN:L2N46A047 TEXT:"pesquisas divulgadas na véspera"] da votação deste domingo mostraram um empate técnico com vantagem numérica de Flávio sobre Lula de no máximo dois pontos nos votos válidos, com 51% a 49%. "Flávio é ligeiramente favorito, ele não é francamente favorito", disse o cientista político Carlos Melo, do Insper. "Quando você olha para as pesquisas, mais do que o número você tem que olhar para a tendência. A tendência é o Flávio caindo, ou praticamente paralisado, e o Lula subindo muito devagar", acrescentou, apontando que não é possível prever se essa tendência resultará em uma virada a favor de Lula neste domingo. Um dos fatores cruciais a ser observado, na avaliação de Melo, será o comparecimento às urnas, já que historicamente o eleitorado que tende a apoiar mais Lula e o PT costuma ter um comparecimento menor. Não à toa, a campanha de Lula vem concentrando esforços em incentivar pessoas que não votaram no primeiro turno a comparecerem na seção eleitoral neste domingo. No primeiro turno, mais de 33,4 milhões de eleitores não foram votar, uma abstenção de 21,08%, em um total de mais de 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar. Neste domingo, no entanto, foi Flávio Bolsonaro quem fez um apelo para que os eleitores compareçam às urnas. "Faça chuva ou faça sol, bora sair de casa para votar, que o Brasil vai mudar e o Brasil vai vencer", disse o senador, após votar no Rio de Janeiro. "Chegou a hora da mudança de verdade", afirmou o candidato, ao lado da esposa Fernanda e da mãe, Rogéria. As três semanas de campanha do segundo turno foram bastante diferentes dos meses que antecederam o primeiro turno, realizado no dia 4 de outubro. No caso de Lula, uma guinada em direção a uma mobilização maciça nas redes sociais e em eventos de rua, que ocorreu sem participação direta do núcleo duro da campanha no primeiro turno, contrastou com uma primeira fase de campanha que o próprio Lula reconheceu em reunião do PT como a "menos organizada" de que participou desde 1989. Na véspera da eleição, antes de participar de evento de campanha em Copacabana, Lula afirmou que "o povo assumiu para si a responsabilidade de fazer a campanha". Um dos destaques da campanha petista no segundo turno foi o impulso nas redes, liderada pelo canal de WhatsApp "Exército do Lula", criado pelo deputado federal reeleito André Janones (Rede-MG), que juntou mais de 10 milhões de pessoas para ouvir as "missões" que Janones dá para os apoiadores cumprirem nas redes. A campanha de Flávio chegou a entrar no TSE pedindo a suspensão do canal. A guinada digital da campanha petista teve como ápice Lula, um crítico público do uso frequente de celular que se orgulhava de não ter o aparelho, ganhando um de presente do governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles (PT), e passando a fazer vários vídeos no formato selfie para apoiadores. Do lado de Flávio, após a inesperada liderança no dia 4, o senador deu declarações que geraram polêmica, como quando disse que, se eleito, usará a força que terá no próximo Congresso para alterar a Constituição. Posteriormente, afirmou que iria propor mudanças constitucionais como o fim da reeleição e a redução da maioridade penal. Também acabou mudando de posição em temas pautados por Lula, como o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1, ao qual ele votou a favor no Senado, apesar de, num passado muito recente, ter se declarado contrário. O senador, por outro lado, também conseguiu mobilizar grandes públicos em atos de campanha em todo o país, no que foi uma marca da campanha de ambos os lados. Na véspera da eleição, e em meio à previsão de chuvas fortes nas regiões Sul e Sudeste, onde Flávio teve desempenho melhor que Lula, o senador usou suas redes sociais para incentivar as pessoas a irem votar. "Pega alguém que não foi votar no primeiro turno e leva para votar no segundo. Compareça às urnas neste segundo turno, independente do tempo, faça chuva, faça sol, não deixe de sair de casa para votar, cada voto é muito importante", afirmou ele em vídeo publicado em sua conta no Instagram. JUDICIALIZAÇÃO Em uma campanha marcada por grande movimentação das duas campanhas contra os adversários no TSE, que levou o presidente da corte Kassio Nunes Marques, a pedir que as campanhas moderassem a quantidade de ações, há receios de que, independentemente do vencedor, ocorram novos embates mesmo após a declaração do resultado. A expectativa de uma margem apertada a favor do eleito também leva a crer que isso possa ocorrer. "A expectativa é de que vai ser uma eleição tensa", disse Creomar de Souza, analista político da Dharma Political Risk. "Acho que a gente ainda vai ter algum nível de discussão política, algum nível de embate jurídico", avaliou. Tanto Flávio quanto Lula não hesitaram em se acusar mutuamente de ladrão, corrupto e mentiroso ao longo de uma campanha em que propostas e discussões sobre o país ficaram em segundo plano. Denúncias de irregularidades contra os candidatos e seus familiares foram amplamente explorados, levando, nos últimos dias, a uma guerra de narrativas sobre a abertura de sigilos das duas partes. Em uma eleição que mais uma vez marcou a importância das redes sociais no processo político, a Meta (META.O) , proprietária do Facebook, do Instagram e do WhatsApp também ficou no foco, após a campanha de Lula apontar que teve sua atuação restrita nas plataformas da empresa, levando a big tech norte-americana a prestar esclarecimentos ao TSE.

item.title: ¿Cuándo sale GTA 6? Fecha, hora de lanzamiento y cuándo empieza la descarga anticipada
item.description: La nueva entrega de Grand Theft Auto ha generado tanta expectativa que se espera frene la economía el día de su salida.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Garrido
item.content:encoded: Tras casi un año de retraso, este noviembre finalmente llegará “GTA 6”, un videojuego que ha mantenido la expectativa por varios meses. Originalmente previsto para 2025, Rockstar Games decidió aplazar su lanzamiento para ofrecer un título que valiera la espera de más de 10 años desde la salida de su predecesor. La sexta entrega de la saga Grand Theft Auto saldrá el 19 de noviembre tanto para Playstation 5 como para la Xbox Series X|S, anunció Rockstar Games. Para ambas consolas estarán disponibles en una versión estándar en US$79,99 y la Ultimate Edition que incluye contenido adicional por US$99,99. La compañía no lanzará una versión física del título. Aunque se comercializará un formato en estuche, este solo tendrá un código de descarga. Tanto en la tienda de Xbox como la de Playstation, los fanáticos podrán descargar “GTA 6” desde la media noche del 19 de noviembre, según los sitios oficiales. Las tiendas indican que se desbloqueará a la medianoche de cada región, aunque Rockstar todavía no ha confirmado oficialmente si habrá un horario unificado. De este modo, algunos jugadores podrían comenzar a tener acceso antes que otros. La expectativa es tal, que especialistas han señalado que el ausentismo laboral por jugar el día del lanzamiento podría costarle a la economía US$1.000 millones . IGN incluso está realizando una encuesta en la que más del 40% de los usuarios dicen que ya pidieron el día libre. Rockstar Games dio a conocer que quienes reserven el juego podrán descargarlo de forma anticipada el 12 de noviembre, una semana antes del lanzamiento. Sin embargo, el título podrá jugarse hasta el día de su salida. El estudio también informó que cualquier versión adquirida en preventa brindará acceso a Vintage Vice City Pack, que contiene varios artículos digitales retro. Junto con la llegada de la nueva entrega de “Grand Theft Auto”, estarán disponibles un soundtrack en formato de disco de vinil así como una caja de artículos coleccionables inspirado en el universo del juego.

item.title: Uganda to impose 21-day quarantine on returning citizens with Congo travel history
item.description: Ugandan citizens returning to the country with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said on Sunday as Uganda tightened Ebola precautions despite saying it remained Ebola-free.
item.dc:creator: Elias Biryabarema
item.content:encoded: Ugandan citizens returning to the country with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said on Sunday as Uganda tightened Ebola precautions despite saying it remained Ebola-free. Uganda has been investigating a Nigerian Ebola case involving a woman who had travelled from Uganda. Officials said they were reviewing genomic sequencing, travel information, interactions and movements in coordination with Nigerian authorities and international partners. Baryomunsi said on Sunday that all 60 contacts linked to a [USN:L6N469174 TEXT:"Kenyan Ebola case"] had completed their 21-day monitoring period and been discharged. The contacts were traced across points of entry and exit, hotels and transport operators linked to travellers' movements through Uganda. "The ministry has intensified traveller screening at Entebbe International Airport and all land border crossings. All travellers intending to enter Uganda by air, land or water must complete the passenger locator form," he said. [USN:L1N46915U TEXT:"Genomic analysis"] of Nigeria's only confirmed Ebola case showed the virus was closely related to the strain detected in Kenya's index case, though Nigerian authorities said there was no evidence that the Kenya case travelled to Nigeria or had a direct connection. Uganda borders Congo, where the outbreak began, and has previously battled Ebola outbreaks.

item.title: HDFC Bank launches flexible EV car loan with longer battery repayment
item.description: The Flexi Electric Car Loan offers separate financing for the vehicle body and battery, allowing customers to customise EMIs and repay the battery portion over a longer tenure ...
item.dc:creator: Our Bureau
item.content:encoded: HDFC Bank, India’s largest private sector lender, on Sunday said it had launched the “Flexi Electric Car Loan”, which finances the body and battery of an electric vehicle (EV) in different proportions and allows the battery portion to be repaid over a longer term. The bank described the product as the first of its kind and said the structure allows customers to customise their equated monthly instalment (EMI) outflow. Batteries are the costliest component of an EV, making these vehicles more expensive to acquire than internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, the bank said. The EMI on the battery portion will be comparable to the running cost of an ICE vehicle, it said, adding that the approach aligns with evolving battery subscription models. The loan is meant only for EV purchases and covers vehicles from leading original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). It is available at the bank’s more than 9,700 branches. “The EV revolution in India is fast gaining momentum, supported by government incentives, a push for an improved technological landscape and judicious policies. HDFC Bank’s Flexi Electric Car Loan is one more step in that direction as India is set to embrace the EV revolution. Further, we believe the Flexi Electric Car Loan will play a pivotal role in making EV ownership a cost-effective, seamless and hassle-free journey,” said Arvind Vohra, group head, retail assets and rural banking, HDFC Bank.

item.title: Real Madrid goalkeeper Courtois to miss Clasico due to illness
item.description: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss his side's LaLiga fixture at Barcelona on Sunday due to the flu, the club said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss his side's LaLiga fixture at Barcelona on Sunday due to the flu, the club said in a statement. Courtois' absence leaves manager Jose Mourinho without a key player for a vital clash with their league-leading rivals. The 34-year-old Belgian will miss his first game this season. Andriy Lunin is in line to replace Courtois in goal at Camp Nou. Lunin's last appearance for Real Madrid came on May 3, in a 2-0 win over Espanyol. Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the senior squad, with Sergio Mestre the other goalkeeper in the matchday squad.

item.title: Newlands to provide test of more than bat and ball for Australia
item.description: The third test will be held at the scene of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal.
item.dc:creator: Nick Said
item.content:encoded: Australia return to the scene of one of the darkest days in the country’s cricket history when the series-deciding third test against South Africa starts at Newlands on Tuesday. The battle may be mental as much as one of skill for several of the Australian players, not least former captain Steve Smith, who was at the centre of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal in 2018. Current skipper Pat Cummins was part of that side, as were fellow seamer Josh Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon, though they say they had no knowledge of the attempt to alter the condition of the ball with a piece of sandpaper. Smith bore the brunt of the considerable fallout in Australia eight years ago and having not reached the heights he might have expected on this tour, averaging a little over 20 with the bat, he would see this as the perfect time to put that right. There has so far been little chatter in South Africa about Sandpapergate but that could change at Newlands, where the first three days’ ticket sales have been strong after sparse crowds at the first two tests in Durban and Gqeberha. "He'll be fine," Australia opener Travis Head said of Smith. "I think he showed that in 2019 in England. We support him. He's been through a lot in that space and handles it well. Sometimes it brings the best out of him, as we've seen in the past." The series is level at 1-1 after big wins for both sides in the opening two games and Australia wicketkeeper Alex Carey told reporters on Sunday that it looked to be another good test-match pitch. "We are still a couple of days out but it looks another great surface," he said. "If you look back at Durban it was a five-day test match and a great contest between bat and ball. The same in Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha) and this should be no different." There has never been a test match played at Newlands in October, and just three in November, all against Australia. The tourists won the first two in 1902 and 1921, but the most recent November fixture was an eight-wicket victory for South Africa in 2011 when Australia were famously bowled out for 47 in their second innings. South Africa will be without fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who injured his groin in the second test. Captain Temba Bavuma said they would pick horses for courses in terms of his replacement. "You’ve got guys like Gerald (Coetzee), Pato (Dane Paterson), as well as (Corbin) Bosch, and we have Sen (Senuran Muthusamy) as well, so the options are there," he said. "Whoever we decide, we’ll be confident they form part of our best XI for the conditions."

Amazon frontier town backs Flávio Bolsonaro as land rights fuel fight over Brazil’s forests

Novo Progresso, where Liberal Party presidential candidate won 84.13% in the first round, is campaigning for a 90% vote share in Sunday’s runoff.

Fabiano Maisonnave

25 October, 2026 03:57 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Leia em português.Lea la nota en español

“We have been fighting against the environment.”

That is how Rosana Gonzaga, the vice mayor of Novo Progresso, explains the Amazon frontier town becoming one of Brazil’s strongest bastions of support for conservative presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.

Show Full Article

A cattle rancher affiliated with Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party, Gonzaga named President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Brazil’s former Environment Minister Marina Silva among the town’s adversaries in a two-decade fight over protected land.

Gonzaga is now helping lead a campaign to give Flávio Bolsonaro 90% of Novo Progresso’s votes in Sunday’s presidential runoff, after he won 84.13% there in the election’s first round. It was the second-highest vote share for the candidate among Brazil’s 5,569 municipalities. The goal of local bolsonaristas is for Novo Progresso to give him the strongest support in the country in the second round.

The runoff on Sunday presents a stark divide over the Amazon rainforest and the environment. Lula, a leftist, has pledged to end net deforestation — Brazil’s largest source of carbon emissions — by 2030 and has tied his agenda to Brazil’s Paris Agreement commitments. Flávio Bolsonaro has questioned human-caused climate change and pledged to eliminate only illegal deforestation, leaving room for legally authorized forest-clearing. The race remains extremely close, with polls showing a technical tie. In the first round, the conservative candidate led 47% to 45.2%.

In Novo Progresso, Bolsonaro supporters have printed “90%” t-shirts and bumper stickers and organized a motorcade of pickups, cars, motorcycles and even excavators, which was joined by the governor-elect of Para state, Daniel Santos. Gonzaga wrapped her car in campaign imagery showing her alongside Flávio Bolsonaro, his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro — convicted over an attempted coup and serving his sentence under house arrest — and Jair’s wife, Senator-elect Michelle Bolsonaro.

The car bore the slogan, “I voted for the father, I’m voting for the son.”

Gonzaga’s family moved to Novo Progresso, in southern Para state, in 2003. They bought an area of primary forest from a private seller even though the land itself belonged to the federal government and came without formal title. Then, three years later, Lula’s government included it in a new conservation area. Gonzaga says the designation left the family and other farmers without access to credit and exposed them to fines and enforcement actions.

Her family story follows a model that has shaped Brazil for decades, if not centuries: Settlers of European descent pushing the agricultural frontier deeper into the country’s interior. In the Amazon, that expansion has taken place across vast stretches of undesignated public land. Land grabbers identify and take over those areas, clear the forest and create a paper trail for plots of land before selling them. States and the federal government often normalized such occupations, creating incentives for the practice to continue.

During Lula’s first term, his government, with Marina Silva as environment minister, sought to make the Novo Progresso region a showcase for slowing deforestation. The town sits along the BR-163 highway, important as an export corridor for soy produced in neighboring Mato Grosso state. To prevent forest loss from spreading along the route — the most common pattern of deforestation in the Amazon — the government rolled out a package of measures that included designating protected areas and tightening environmental enforcement.

In 2006, it created the Jamanxim National Forest, placing Gonzaga’s farm and several others inside a federal conservation area. In Brazil, national forests are publicly owned and intended only for sustainable use of native vegetation and scientific research. Gonzaga has since become one of the leaders of a movement seeking to privatize about 486,000 hectares (1.2 million acres) within this protected zone, roughly six times the area of New York City, a goal Flávio Bolsonaro has pledged to advance.

“I’m going to carry out the largest land regularization Para has ever seen,” he said during a visit to the city of Maraba on Monday. “Your land will be yours on paper.” He added, “We’re going to get rid of the environmental restrictions that exist for ideological reasons.”

During the four years of his term as president, Jair Bolsonaro didn’t push to legalize the settlers’ lands, but his weakening of environmental law enforcement led to a surge in deforestation. From 2019 through 2022, a period that largely overlaps his presidency, about 52,300 hectares were deforested inside Jamanxim National Forest, nearly double the area recorded in the period 2015 through  2018. From 2023 through 2026, under Lula, deforestation fell by about 86%, according to official data.

In 2019, Novo Progresso became a symbol of Jair Bolsonaro’s lax approach to the Amazon after local farmers organized coordinated fires to show support for his government and, according to reports at the time, in an effort to make satellite monitoring of deforestation more difficult. The episode made headlines across the world and became known as the “Day of Fire.”

After his reelection to a third term, Lula reinstated environmental law enforcement across the Amazon but also tried to build bridges with Novo Progresso and other cities with high deforestation rates. The government in 2024 launched the Union with Municipalities, a program that combines land-tenure and environmental reform with technical assistance to help family farmers access public programs and credit.

But the program had little impact, according to the mayor of Novo Progresso, Gelson Dill, a center-right politician who is not aligned with Bolsonaro. The town received some of the promised investment, he said, but not enough, and the initiative never became the “turning point” in the municipality’s relationship with the federal government that officials had hoped for.

Dill agrees that the region needs to legalize land already used for farming, including in Jamanxim. But as Bolsonaro supporters anticipate a change in environmental policy, the mayor also sees a risk.

“I hope this expectation around the new government doesn’t bring any rush to deforest here,” he said.

item.title: Pacers expect more of themselves, look to regroup vs. winless Nets
item.description: Getting a win in guard Tyrese Haliburton's return to the court was emotional and joyful, but the follow-up was a massive letdown for the Indiana Pacers, especially in the opening 24 minutes.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Getting a win in guard Tyrese Haliburton's return to the court was emotional and joyful, but the follow-up was a massive letdown for the Indiana Pacers, especially in the opening 24 minutes. Two nights after getting outclassed in the first half, the Pacers hope their performance is vastly improved Sunday night when they visit the winless Brooklyn Nets. Haliburton has scored 41 points and handed out 19 assists in his first two games after missing all of last season with a torn right Achilles tendon. The star point guard returned with a double-double during a 123-120 win in the season opener at New Orleans before scoring 18 in Friday's 121-105 loss to the Dallas Mavericks in Indiana's home opener. While the final margin was only 16 points, the Pacers were much worse in the opening half. Indiana allowed 77 points in the first half and trailed by as many as 37. Against New Orleans, Indiana allowed 66 points in the first half. Through two games, the Pacers have been outscored by 44 points before halftime. "It just simply comes down to an attitude and a disposition," Pacers coach Rick Carlisle said. "And two straight games, we haven't had it the way we need to have it in the first half. "It's not OK, and we all own it. Every single one of us. Start with me. I didn't have these guys ready to play the way they needed to be ready to play." Indiana is hoping to avoid giving up 44 points in the first quarter like it did on Friday when Dallas wound up shooting 69.6% from the floor (16 of 23) and hitting 8 of 13 3-point tries (61.5%). "There's obviously a lot of room for us to grow," Haliburton said. "We've got to be better. And I really put it on that first five. We've got to be a lot better in that starting group." Forward Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 23 points after getting 30 in the season opener, but Indiana would like more consistency from center Ivica Zubac, who was held to nine after getting 16 in the season opener. The Nets are trying to avoid losing their first three games for the second straight season. Last season, the Nets lost their first three by a combined 37 points as part of a seven-game skid en route to a 62-loss season. Brooklyn's two losses are by a combined 11 points, and the Nets nearly erased a 22-point deficit in Saturday's 125-121 loss at Cleveland. Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle have been Brooklyn's leading scorers in each game and are hoping to see more help like the duo got in the second half. Porter led the Nets with 28 points and Randle added 23 while second-year guard Egor Demin contributed 15 of his 22 points in the fourth quarter. Brooklyn scored 41 points and hit nine of its 16 3-point attempts in the fourth. "I think it was the shot quality," Nets coach Jordi Fernandez said. "We went from taking 35 good shots in the first half to almost 50 in the second. When you take the high-quality shots, they don't all go in at the same time, but then if you keep shooting them, we had that stretch that they kept going in." The Nets will likely have a slightly different lineup because rookie Mikel Brown Jr. will sit on the second night of a back-to-back. Brown shot 3-for-10, scored eight points in 20 minutes and shared the court with Demin in the fourth. But the guard, the sixth overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, also dealt with an ankle issue in the preseason and is on a minutes restriction. --Field Level Media

item.title: Senegal party that controls parliament comes out against revised budget bill
item.description: Senegal's Pastef party, which holds a large majority in the National Assembly, said it would not pass the government's revised budget, reinforcing doubts over how quickly the country can push ahead with its debt restructuring.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Senegal's Pastef party, which holds a large majority in the National Assembly, said it would not pass the government's revised budget, reinforcing doubts over how quickly the country can push ahead with its debt restructuring . A statement by the party headed by former Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko cited "disagreements over certain budgetary decisions, the chosen financing arrangements and the insufficient guarantees provided to parliament", though it said the party was open to engaging with the government on getting a new budget in place The West African nation has been grappling with a debt burden that had reached 132% of gross domestic product by the end of 2024, International Monetary Fund figures show, after the government uncovered billions of dollars in [USN:L8N3TJ1N8 TEXT:"misreported borrowing"] by the previous administration The government reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF in early September for a $2.2 billion, 36-month Extended Credit Facility to support its reform program. But without parliamentary approval of the revised budget, the government risks delaying the IMF program, which underpins its entire debt restructuring strategy Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo plans to hold a press conference on Sunday to discuss the revised budget "which is intended to implement a revised framework aimed at improving the quality of life of Senegalese people" The amended 2026 budget bill paints a sharply deteriorating fiscal picture. It cuts real GDP growth to 2.7% from roughly 5% in the original budget and widens the deficit to 7.6% of GDP from 5.4%, driven largely by a tripling of energy subsidies to 790.3 billion CFA francs ($1.36 billion) from 250 billion

item.title: Beirut's $13 chicken sandwich becomes symbol of Lebanon divide
item.description: Seven years after Lebanon’s devastating financial meltdown, a debate over a chicken sandwich has exposed an increasingly stark divide between those who can still spend freely and those struggling to get by.
item.dc:creator: Nazih Osseiran, Raghed Waked, Emilie Madi
item.content:encoded: Seven years after Lebanon’s [USN:L6N41Y0N8 TEXT:"devastating financial meltdown"], a debate over a chicken sandwich has exposed an increasingly stark divide between those who can still spend freely and those struggling to get by. A trendy health restaurant wanted to offer its calorie-conscious customers a healthier take on the beloved Levantine wrap known as the shish taouk. So, The Glow Paradise launched the “Chic Taouk”, pricing it at around $13 — nearly double what an un-chic chicken sandwich typically goes for in Beirut. The pricy pun proved hard to swallow, with outraged critics accusing the restaurant of overcharging in a country where many households struggle to afford basic necessities. Yet while the debate raged on social media, customers kept buying. The Glow Paradise sold more than 20,000 Chic Taouk sandwiches in just 11 days, according to managing partner Hrag Jeghalian, who described the online exchanges as "natural marketing". The contrasting reactions touched a nerve in Lebanon, where years of financial turmoil, political dysfunction and conflict have reshaped the country's social landscape, hollowing out much of the middle class while leaving a smaller group of consumers able to sustain an affluent lifestyle. DEBATE PULLS FOCUS AWAY FROM URGENT CRISES Sami Nader, an economist at the Saint Joseph University of Beirut, said the throngs at The Glow Paradise belied another reality. “So you see people in the restaurant, but what you don't see is that 22 restaurants closed last month,” Nader told Reuters. Lebanon’s Instagram-active community was split between those accusing the restaurant of theft and others saying the sandwich was intended for those who could afford it. Some questioned whether the dispute itself reflected misplaced priorities in a country grappling with urgent crises, from Israel’s[USN:L6N45P03S TEXT:" occupation"] of large swaths of the country’s south to the endemic electricity and water crises. Lebanon’s 2019 financial collapse was prompted by decades of corruption and profligate spending by the ruling elite, and several rounds of conflict since then have worsened the country’s economic outlook. GDP has declined by nearly 40% since 2019 and inflation is expected to rise to 17.5% due to rising global energy and shipping prices eating away at people’s purchasing power, according to the World Bank. The figure is more than quadruple the [USN:L1N43A0MP TEXT:"global headline inflation"] rate flagged by the International Monetary Fund in July. Four in five households in Lebanon struggle to afford basic necessities, the UN children’s agency said in September. 'PEOPLE CAN'T KEEP UP' The country’s middle class has “disappeared,” Nader said, dismantled by a series of crises including the collapse of the financial system in 2019, the 2020 Beirut Port explosion and two wars in under two years. Monthly bills from private generator operators, which provide electricity to many homes and businesses during outages on Lebanon's failing national grid, jumped by nearly 20% in August 2026 alone, bringing rates nearly 60% higher than they were in February of this year, according to the kilowatt-hour prices set by Lebanon’s energy ministry. For many, that means paying for 24/7 electricity now costs several hundred dollars a month, in a country where the minimum wage is set at $400. “Everything has become expensive, and people can’t keep up,” said Fouad Fakhreddine, a 53-year-old restaurant worker from nearby Hamra. “We are now getting paid, then getting in debt over that just to get by.” The years of economic instability, he said, have produced “a class that is living, and a class that is not dead and waiting to die from the unbearable situation it is in.” (This story has been refiled to change the name in the byline to Emilie Madi from Ahmad Al Kerdi.)

item.title: Four ways US foreign policy could change if Democrats win in November
item.description: Nonpartisan analysts say Democrats stand a good chance of winning the US House of Representatives and possibly the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, which would give them a slice of power in Washington after two years of Republican control.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: Nonpartisan analysts say Democrats stand a good chance of winning the US House of Representatives and possibly the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections , which would give them a slice of power in Washington after two years of Republican control. Democrats argue that Republicans have allowed President Donald Trump 's administration to declare war and control spending, even though the US Constitution reserves those powers for lawmakers. Here are some ways a Democratic Congress could hem in Trump's foreign policy. CURB THE IRAN WAR Trump did not secure approval from Congress before he launched the war with Iran on February 28, and Democrats have voted repeatedly to end the fighting unless he does so. One of these [USN:L1N42H0RZ TEXT:"resolutions passed"] with support from a handful of Republicans, but Trump's administration ignored it. With control of the House or the Senate, Democrats could cut defense spending to pressure Trump to obtain permission from Congress to continue the war. They could also require administration officials to testify publicly about their plans. FRESH SUPPORT FOR UKRAINE Trump has largely halted direct US financial and military aid to Ukraine, despite broad support from Democratic and Republican lawmakers as it fights a Russian invasion . Most recently, he has angered members of Congress, including many Republicans, by [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"lifting sanctions on Russian diesel"] and waiving sanctions on Russian energy only weeks after signing them into law. With a victory in both chambers in November, Democrats would be able to decide what gets voted on and when. That could allow them to approve new aid to Ukraine, which likely would pass with the two-thirds majorities needed to overcome a Trump veto. They could also target other Trump activities. For example, Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, who could head the House Foreign Affairs Committee if Democrats win control, has introduced bipartisan legislation to block Trump's plan to bring Russian diesel back into the global market. END MILITARY AID TO ISRAEL Support for Israel has plummeted among Democrats over its conduct in the Gaza war , which has killed tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians. The ongoing violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's close alliance with Republicans have also been factors. Democrats could limit or end military aid to Israel, which amounted to $3.8 billion in the most recent fiscal year. That is more than was provided to any other country. Nearly half of House Democrats voted this summer to cut off aid to Israel. Some of those who voted against that effort, such as Meeks, have backed limits on providing weapons like heavy bombs to Israel. LIMIT MILITARY SPENDING AND RESTORE FOREIGN AID Democrats are far more likely than Trump's Republicans to limit military spending. Trump asked for an unprecedented 67% increase in the military budget this year, to $1.5 trillion, but Democrats blocked it in the Senate, citing his refusal to consult Congress about the Iran war and his steep cuts to social programs. Trump has also withheld or canceled billions of dollars in foreign aid approved by Congress. Many Democrats have been angered by the cuts and say they will try to restore funding.

item.title: Rupee's recovery faces hurdles from dollar demand, capital outflows
item.description: The rupee's weakness is being driven by more than the West Asia conflict and elevated crude oil prices, with rising global borrowing costs, changes in importer and exporter hedging behaviour, and ...
item.dc:creator: Anjali Kumari
item.content:encoded: There is more to it in the rupee weakness than the West Asia conflict and elevated crude oil prices alone. The rising global borrowing costs, changes in importer and exporter hedging behaviour, and capital outflows have added to the pressure on the domestic currency. The rupee has appreciated 0.93 per cent in October so far, but has depreciated 0.14 per cent in the current financial year. The recent recovery proved short-lived, with the currency ending an eight-session winning streak on Thursday as rising crude oil prices amid tensions in West Asia renewed pressure. The rupee extended its losses on Friday to close at 94.94 per dollar, against 94.83 in the previous session. The currency had risen from 96.73 per dollar on October 9, close to its all-time low of 96.96 touched in May, to an intraday high of 94.33, aided by dollar inflows linked to the Jio Platforms initial public offering (IPO). However, the gains came amid active intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in the spot and non-deliverable forwards markets. The RBI’s foreign exchange reserves fell by $5.01 billion to $721.02 billion in the week ended October 16. State-owned banks were also buying dollars for oil companies on the central bank’s behalf. The RBI has rolled out several measures to ease pressure on the currency. These include a special dollar window, operational from October 12, to meet the daily dollar requirements of Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation through designated banks. The central bank also tightened rules for banks’ foreign exchange derivative positions and opened concessional swap windows linked to foreign currency non-resident (bank) deposits, overseas foreign currency borrowings and external commercial borrowings. The RBI also raised the repo rate by 25 basis points (bps) to 5.5 per cent on October 7. However, the pressure on the rupee reflects broader shifts in global capital flows and domestic hedging behaviour. Expansionary fiscal policies and an artificial intelligence (AI)-led investment boom in the US have increased competition for capital, pushing up global borrowing costs. “The pressure on the rupee is led by elevated global bond yields, surge in crude oil prices and lately focus on AI-related investments,” said Gaura Sen Gupta, chief economist at IDFC FIRST Bank. The pressure is not limited to India, as the rising cost of capital is affecting emerging markets more broadly, she said. Domestically, expectations of further rupee depreciation have prompted importers to hedge their dollar payables, while exporters have held back from hedging their dollar receipts. This has increased demand for dollars in the market. The RBI’s foreign exchange risk reserve (FERR) framework seeks to address pressures arising from hedging activity. Dislocations in the forward market have added to volatility. Abhishek Goenka, founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of IFA Global, said dollar flows linked to the Jio Platforms IPO and associated funding swaps had widened the basis between spot and forward exchange rates. “Investors sell dollars in cash to subscribe to the IPO and book a forward to hedge currency risk,” Goenka said. These transactions, alongside the RBI’s sell-buy swaps to absorb surplus rupee liquidity from the banking system, contributed to the widening of the basis. Exporters’ inability to cancel and rebook forward contracts further exacerbated the dislocation. “Basis eased considerably on Thursday, that is, spot went up and forwards came off. However, it is still dislocated and there is further room for it to correct,” Goenka said. He added that the 94.20-94.40 per dollar range was a technically strong support zone for the currency, potentially prompting spot buying interest, particularly with Brent crude above $110 per barrel. The rupee is also facing pressure from India’s external account imbalances. An Axis Bank report said the current account deficit (CAD) was above levels that could be comfortably financed, particularly as higher global interest rates had reduced the amount of the deficit that could be funded through capital flows. “Even with new measures, CAD is well above now financeable levels,” the report said. This has kept India’s basic balance of payments in deficit for several quarters. Elevated forward premiums also point to a reversal of the covered interest parity relationship, reflecting expectations of rupee depreciation and, to some extent, pushing domestic interest rates higher, the report said. Financial outflows through overseas direct investment (ODI) have added to the pressure. RBI data showed that annualised ODI by the financial and business services sector in the current financial year so far was well above levels recorded in earlier periods. And, remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme remained broadly steady. Axis Bank said measures may need to extend beyond the current account to address capital outflows. It also noted that defending the currency through higher interest rates had not proved successful in previous episodes.

item.title: Trump campaigns in Michigan a day after Obama rallies Democrats
item.description: US President Donald Trump will rally Republicans in eastern Michigan on Sunday, a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump will rally Republicans in eastern Michigan on Sunday, a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's midterm elections. Michigan has one of the nation's most competitive US Senate contests, an open-seat race between former Republican Representative Mike Rogers and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed that will help decide control of the chamber. Despite repeatedly attacking El-Sayed from the Oval Office and at rallies across the country, the Republican president had not yet campaigned in Michigan this year. If he wins, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Trump has sought to paint El-Sayed as a Muslim extremist and repeatedly [USN:L1N4620ZA TEXT:"mocked his middle name,"] Mohamed, a common Muslim name. El-Sayed has dismissed the accusation and, in a recent advertisement, defended his religion, saying, "faith is a thing there’s just too little of in Washington". Rogers has alleged without evidence that El-Sayed has [USN:L6N4661FE TEXT:"ties to the Muslim Brotherhood"], one of the Arab world's oldest and most influential Islamist groups. "If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: Are you for America or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?" Rogers said at a debate last week. El-Sayed has denied affiliation with the group and says it is "shameful" for Rogers to question his allegiance to the United States. At Saturday's rally in Detroit, Obama framed the attacks on El-Sayed as an attempt by opponents to make him look "less patriotic and less American than they are." The former president compared it to his experience as the target of [USN:KBN23O2P2 TEXT:"false claims"] that he was born in Kenya. "We have seen this movie before," Obama said. "I starred in it ... This stuff didn't work on me. Not in Michigan. It's not going to work on Abdul." Hours after the Detroit event, Trump dismissed Obama's efforts on behalf of El-Sayed. "Now he’s campaigning for a Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist, who hates Jews and Blacks and AMERICANS and TRUMP, and he is going to lose, also", Trump wrote in an early Sunday morning post on Truth Social. Trump's rally in Port Huron, part of an area of Michigan that he won in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66% of the vote, will also highlight the US-Canada tariff standoff. The trade fight has affected the Detroit-based [USN:L6N44N11O TEXT:"US auto industry,"] prompting Rogers to distance himself from the president's policy. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US Senate and US House of Representatives to overturn Republicans' narrow 53-47 and 218-214 majorities.

item.title: How Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump
item.description: The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump's frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv's supporters fear could threaten vital US support.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: Relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy took a sharp downward turn in recent weeks, with each leader openly criticizing the other. The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump's frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv's supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward. Here's how the relationship soured: WHAT IS THE HISTORY OF TRUMP-ZELENSKIY TENSIONS? Trump has been skeptical of US involvement in Ukraine ever since his first term when, shortly after taking office in early 2017, he was asked to provide lethal aid to Ukraine and approved the sale of Javelin missiles to Kyiv. “Everyone around him wanted him to do it, and they pushed him hard and he eventually signed off on selling them Javelins, very reluctantly,” said a former senior Trump administration official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. “He didn’t consider it a core US interest. It was a European issue.” Trump's first major encounter with Zelenskiy came in a July 2019 phone call in which the Republican president asked the Ukrainian leader to investigate his Democratic rival Joe Biden and his son Hunter, in exchange for military support Congress had authorized. That episode led to Trump's first impeachment. Biden beat Trump in the 2020 presidential election. Trump also has fostered a relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin that runs against the norms of US foreign policy but echoes his warm ties with authoritarian leaders Xi Jinping of China and North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un. “Trump has always wanted better relations with Russia,” the former official said. WHAT DEEPENED THE RIFT BETWEEN THE TWO LEADERS? Trump's current frustration centers on Kyiv's [USN:S8N41C0VK TEXT:"attacks on Russian diesel infrastructure"]. Diesel prices have hit record highs since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, and global energy costs spiked. US lawmakers in Trump's Republican party face voter anger over inflation ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. On September 13, Trump began publicly calling on Ukraine to stop targeting diesel infrastructure. The following week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was also concerned that Ukraine had hit US-linked oil shipments. Ukraine has refused to halt the strikes, saying its long-range drone campaign is its only viable response to nearly five years of Russian bombardment. Moscow was forced in July to ban diesel exports as part of a raft of measures to address domestic fuel shortages. Angered by Zelenskiy’s defiance, Trump on October 9 announced a deal to buy diesel from Moscow, issuing a temporary general license that allows Russian diesel to reach the global market. He also waived sanctions on Russia authorized by a bill he signed into law in September. Suriya Jayanti, a former US official who runs a power sector company in Ukraine, said Russia’s strikes on Ukraine’s power grid have increased, despite Trump unilaterally announcing an [USN:FWN45X008 TEXT:"energy ceasefire"] on October 11. "It is clear to everyone in Kyiv that the goal is not actually an energy ceasefire, but it is really just an effort to hobble Ukraine and give Russia a decisive advantage," said Jayanti, who is also a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council think tank. HAS THE US THREATENED TO CUT OFF SUPPORT TO UKRAINE? Zelenskiy has said Ukrainian military officials had been threatened by US counterparts, who said continuing the energy strikes would lead the US to cut off intelligence sharing. A US official familiar with the situation disputed Kyiv's account. Speaking on condition of anonymity, the US official said there has been no increase in pressure on Ukraine. “We don't have to pressure Zelenskiy. If he wants to make a deal he'll make a deal. I think Putin is putting a ton of pressure on him and he (Zelenskiy) is putting some pressure on Russia but Russia doesn't seem to be minding it as much even though they are getting hit." On Thursday, Trump said he had asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to restore Ukraine’s access to the company's Starlink satellite system. Starlink's disruption temporarily hampered Kyiv's military drone operations and spurred fears that Kyiv would be left defenseless against Russia's attacks going into the winter. WHAT IS THE STATUS OF MOSCOW-KYIV PEACE TALKS? Peace efforts have continued but so far have not yielded tangible results. At talks in Oslo on October 20, Ukraine presented new proposals, and Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner repeated Trump's demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian diesel refineries. The next day, envoy Witkoff – a close friend of Trump's - met Putin in St. Petersburg. Putin agreed to release detained American Stephen Hubbard in what the two countries called a goodwill gesture. Zelenskiy said on Friday that negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US would meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, a possible precursor to a meeting of the three countries’ leaders. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February.

item.title: Satellite lights, Google Trends can help estimate state growth: RBI report
item.description: Combining night-time illumination and Google Trends data reduced errors in quarterly growth estimates by up to 62 per cent across three industrial states ...
item.dc:creator: Anjali Kumari
item.content:encoded: Satellite-based night-time lights data and Google search trends can help estimate quarterly economic growth in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka, reducing errors in growth estimates by up to 62 per cent, according to a report in the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI’s) monthly bulletin. The report was authored by RBI staffers, and the views are those of the authors, not the RBI, it was clarified. The study, titled Nowcasting State-Level Economic Activity in India with Night-Time Light and Google Trends, combines satellite imagery and digital search behaviour to estimate quarterly growth in gross state value added (GSVA). It seeks to address gaps in the availability of timely state-level economic data, as official GSVA figures are released annually, typically with a lag of 12-18 months. The report found that combining the two indicators improved the accuracy of estimates compared with a benchmark model that relied on past GSVA growth. The reduction in the root mean squared error (RMSE), a measure of estimation error, was around 38 per cent for Maharashtra, 54 per cent for Karnataka and nearly 62 per cent for Gujarat. The framework uses night-time light data from NASA’s Black Marble satellite dataset and Google Trends indices across 25 search categories. These include searches related to jobs and education, real estate, shopping, finance, travel and automobiles. The model also incorporates past GSVA growth to generate estimates for the current quarter. Night-time light data captures changes in illumination across a state, which can reflect activity in urban settlements, industrial areas and other locations. Google search trends, meanwhile, provide a measure of digital behaviour and demand-related activity. Together, the indicators offer a more frequent view of economic conditions than annual state income data. The study found a strong relationship between year-on-year (Y-o-Y) growth in night-time light intensity and overall GSVA growth. The correlation was highest in Maharashtra at 0.90, followed by Karnataka at 0.79 and Gujarat at 0.66. The relationship remained strong and statistically significant even after the researchers excluded quarters affected by Covid. The findings suggest that satellite-based illumination can capture broad changes in economic activity, while search trends provide additional information that improves estimates. The study also found that night-time light data carried information useful for predicting subsequent GSVA growth, while Google Trends indicators contributed mainly through signals available in the same period. For the analysis, the researchers processed monthly satellite observations to remove low-quality pixels and background noise before aggregating the data into quarterly measures. They then compared changes in night-time light intensity with official state-level economic growth figures and incorporated the indicators into a statistical model to produce quarterly estimates. The study covered quarterly observations from 2013-14 to the third quarter of 2024-25 for Maharashtra and Karnataka. Gujarat’s series extended up to the fourth quarter of 2023-24 because of data constraints. The model’s performance was tested against a benchmark using an expanding-window approach, in which estimates were generated using information available up to each period. The authors also examined a modified measure of GSVA that excluded sectors such as agriculture, forestry and mining, where economic activity may not be fully reflected in night-time illumination. However, estimates for aggregate GSVA generally performed more consistently, indicating that excluding sectors with lower light intensity did not systematically improve short-term estimates. The study focuses on Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka, selected as major industrial states. The authors said high-frequency regional estimates could help identify changes in economic activity and provide additional information for short-term economic assessment. The framework is intended to supplement official statistics rather than replace them. Its application beyond the three states and further improvements to the modelling approach could help assess how reliably alternative data sources can track economic activity across regions.

item.title: China y Corea del Sur le están arrebatando el mercado colombiano de vehículos a Brasil y México
item.description: Las compras externas de vehículos, partes y accesorios impulsaron las importaciones colombianas entre enero y agosto de 2026. Al mismo tiempo, los híbridos y eléctricos ganaron participación en las ma ...
item.dc:creator: Daniel Guerrero
item.content:encoded: Bogotá — Las importaciones de vehículos están transformando el mercado automotor colombiano. Entre enero y agosto de 2026, las compras externas de automóviles, partes y accesorios crecieron 55,9% frente al mismo periodo de 2025, mientras China consolidó su posición como principal proveedor de vehículos, Corea del Sur casi que creció cinco veces, mientras que Brasil y México perdieron terreno. De acuerdo con ANIF, el cambio ocurre en un contexto de aumento generalizado de las importaciones y recuperación de las matrículas de vehículos nuevos. A esta dinámica se suma una transformación en las preferencias de los compradores, con una participación creciente de los automóviles híbridos y eléctricos en las ventas nacionales. En agosto de 2026, las importaciones totales de Colombia aumentaron 31,7% frente al mismo mes del año anterior, al pasar de US$5.850 millones CIF a US$7.702 millones CIF, según las cifras recogidas por ANIF. El comportamiento prolonga una tendencia ascendente que comenzó a principios de 2025 y que, de acuerdo con el análisis, ha recibido un impulso adicional del comportamiento favorable del peso colombiano frente al dólar. Entre enero y agosto, las importaciones acumularon un crecimiento de 17,2% y alcanzaron US$53.746 millones CIF. Si la trayectoria se mantiene, el año podría cerrar con compras externas cercanas a US$80.000 millones CIF. Entre los principales grupos que contribuyeron al aumento figuran los combustibles, los aceites minerales y sus productos, los productos farmacéuticos y los vehículos, partes y accesorios. Este último segmento registró el mayor aporte al incremento de las importaciones. Frente al mismo periodo de 2025, sus compras externas aumentaron US$2.326 millones CIF, con una variación de 55,9%. El crecimiento también elevó el peso de la industria automotriz dentro de las importaciones totales. Su participación pasó de 9,1% en 2025 a 12,1% en 2026, una proporción superior incluso a la registrada en 2022, cuando representó 7,4% de las compras externas del país. China se consolida como uno de los principales protagonistas de la transformación del mercado automotor colombiano. Según ANIF, el país asiático ya era el principal origen de las mercancías importadas por Colombia en 2025 y continuó ganando participación durante 2026. En el mercado de vehículos automotores, China representó 30,1% de las importaciones con corte a julio de 2026. Cuatro años atrás, en 2022, su participación era de 16,1%. Corea del Sur también aumentó su presencia entre los proveedores de automóviles para Colombia. Su participación pasó de 2,5% en 2022 a 11,6% en 2026. Las ganancias de participación de estos dos países contrastan con la pérdida de terreno de Brasil, que registró la mayor disminución dentro de esta categoría, y de México. Los datos muestran un cambio en la composición geográfica de las compras externas de vehículos. El crecimiento de las importaciones automotrices no solo está aumentando el peso de este sector en el comercio exterior colombiano, sino que también coincide con una mayor participación de los proveedores asiáticos. El aumento de las importaciones ha coincidido con una recuperación de las ventas de vehículos nuevos en Colombia. De acuerdo con las cifras presentadas por ANIF, ambas variables mantienen una evolución ascendente desde enero de 2025. En septiembre de 2026 se registraron 33.890 matrículas nuevas de automóviles, frente a 24.894 en el mismo mes de 2025. Esto representa un crecimiento anual de 36,1%. La recuperación es aún más marcada al comparar el resultado con el de septiembre de 2023, cuando se registraron 15.611 matrículas nuevas. ANIF señala que, durante los dos años anteriores al inicio de la tendencia ascendente, los mayores registros de matrículas respondían principalmente a un comportamiento estacional de fin de año. La evolución observada desde enero de 2025 muestra una dinámica diferente, con un aumento que se ha extendido a lo largo del periodo analizado. El crecimiento de las matrículas coincide, además, con cambios en las preferencias de los consumidores por las tecnologías de propulsión de los vehículos nuevos. La transformación del mercado automotor colombiano también se refleja en la composición de las matrículas según el tipo de tecnología. En 2016, los vehículos a gasolina representaban 87% de las ventas de automóviles nuevos. Al incluir los vehículos diésel, la participación de estas dos tecnologías ascendía a 99%. Diez años después, la distribución es distinta. Aunque los vehículos a gasolina continúan liderando las matrículas, con 38,6% del total entre enero y septiembre de 2026, los híbridos y eléctricos han ganado una participación considerable. Los vehículos híbridos representaron 30,1% de las matrículas nuevas acumuladas entre enero y septiembre, mientras que los eléctricos alcanzaron 16,1%. En conjunto, estas dos tecnologías sumaron 46,2% de las matrículas nuevas durante los primeros nueve meses del año, frente a una participación cercana a 1% que, según el análisis de ANIF, tenían hace una década. La composición de las ventas evidencia el avance de los vehículos híbridos y eléctricos dentro del mercado colombiano. Su participación conjunta ya supera la de los automóviles a gasolina considerados individualmente.
