item.title: Le suspect de l'attaque dans les Yvelines placé en observation psychiatrique
item.description: Le suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été placé en observation psychiatrique, le temps d'apprécier si son état de santé est compatible avec la poursuite des auditions, a annoncé dimanche le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été placé en observation psychiatrique, le temps d'apprécier si son état de santé est compatible avec la poursuite des auditions, a annoncé dimanche le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT). Ce placement en observation psychiatrique peut durer 48 heures et la garde à vue du suspect est suspendue durant cette période, a précisé le PNAT. Une analyse toxicologique a en outre permis de révéler la présence de cannabis et de cocaïne dans le sang de cet homme, a ajouté le PNAT. Les gardes à vue des membres de son entourage familial et amical se poursuivent. A la suite de cette attaque contre des passants commise à l'aide d'une arme automatique, le PNAT a ouvert une enquête du chef de "tentatives d'assassinats en relation avec une entreprise terroriste, avec la circonstance que les faits ont été commis à raison de l’appartenance vraie ou supposée, à une prétendue race, une ethnie, une nation ou une religion déterminée". Le président de la République Emmanuel Macron a qualifié cette attaque d'"attentat terroriste" à "caractère raciste avéré".

item.title: Jordan church attack survivor says her cousin died before her eyes
item.description: When gunmen opened fire on a church in Jordan, Sahar al-Halsa hid behind a pillar as she heard the shooting and people screaming in panic during a funeral service for her cousin's daughter.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
item.content:encoded: When gunmen opened fire on a church in Jordan, Sahar al-Halsa hid behind a pillar as she heard the shooting and people screaming in panic during a funeral service for her cousin's daughter. When she rushed outside in the chaos, she said she spotted the assailants and another cousin lying on the ground wounded. "I went to him and said: 'Assem, Assem, my darling, answer me'," she said. She said he opened his eyes to look at her, but then "he was gone". Friday's attack on the Greek Orthodox place of worship in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman, prompted King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, to order security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to what authorities described as extremist terrorism. PRIEST SENDS MESSAGE OF LOVE AND PEACE Nine people died in the shooting that witnesses said lasted for several minutes. The funeral services were held on Sunday. Eight of the victims’ coffins were wrapped in Jordanian flags before they were buried in a graveyard in the village of Hamoud, where the attack took place. Mourners and priests gathered at the scene. Forty people were wounded in the rare attack on minority Christians. Speaking from her home, from where the red dome of St George's church is visible, al-Halsa concluded that God must have saved her. "My life starts now, because I was going to die," she said, speaking beside her husband Ziad al-Halsa. A statue of Jesus on a cross was displayed on a shelf. Authorities have said they are still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. There has been no immediate claim of responsibility. Ziad said he ran the short distance to the church after he heard the gunfire, describing the overwhelming sense of relief when he realised Sahar, who he described as "the love of his life", was safe. "To my cousins, may God have mercy on them," he said. Such attacks are highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities there say they have foiled several Islamist plots in recent years. Speaking ahead of the funerals, priest Yuhanna Hamati said: "Our message from this church, from this place where this horrific crime was committed, is a message of love, peace, and reassurance. A message that we send to the whole world."

item.title: Employees group warns of major Swiss job losses if UBS relocates
item.description: As many as 12,000 UBS jobs in Switzerland could be at risk if tougher capital rules prompt the bank to relocate, according to the Swiss Bank Employees Association, or SBPV.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As many as 12,000 UBS (UBSG.S) jobs in Switzerland could be at risk if tougher capital rules prompt the bank to relocate, according to the Swiss Bank Employees Association, or SBPV. In a letter to lawmakers first published at the weekend by newspaper NZZ am Sonntag, the association warned that a relocation, sale or merger of UBS could cost 10,000 to 12,000 of UBS's roughly 34,000 jobs in Switzerland. The letter, which was also seen by Reuters, described this as the "worst case" scenario, and comes on top of cuts already made at the bank as it completes it integration of fallen rival Credit Suisse, which it acquired in 2023. UBS, which has repeatedly said it wants to remain in Switzerland, declined to comment on the SBPV estimate. A UBS spokesperson said the bank would keep job cuts resulting from the Credit Suisse takeover as low as possible. UBS said it still expects around 3,000 layoffs in Switzerland under the integration and that these would occur over several years, largely via steps like natural turnover, early retirements and insourcing of jobs once held externally. The SBPV warning comes as a committee in the lower house of the Swiss parliament [USN:L1N45N0NB TEXT:"prepares"] to discuss how much capital UBS should have to hold to back its foreign subsidiaries. Last month, the upper house [USN:L8N45F0DE TEXT:"proposed"] UBS should back those units with 90% Common Equity Tier 1 capital. UBS suggested that is [USN:L1N45C05I TEXT:"too much"] and the bank's chairman has warned it would need to carefully [USN:L8N4590WE TEXT:"consider"] its future in Switzerland if the rules are too harsh. Some shareholders of the bank have called for UBS to [USN:L1N45N061 TEXT:"leave"] Switzerland, and the bank has been [USN:L1N46205Q TEXT:"drafting"] potential contingency plans including shifting its headquarters or merging with another lender, sources have told Reuters. The SBPV letter, which also said UBS had a duty to commit to its Swiss base, urged lawmakers to pursue a "viable compromise" that did not impose such a heavy burden on the bank.

item.title: Clinical Catlin triumphs in Hong Kong Open
item.description: American John Catlin showed nerves of steel as he held local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finnish opponent Kalle Samooja at bay to win the Hong Kong Open, hitting seven birdies in Sunday's final round to finish five strokes ahead of his nearest challengers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: American John Catlin showed nerves of steel as he held local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finnish opponent Kalle Samooja at bay to win the Hong Kong Open, hitting seven birdies in Sunday's final round to finish five strokes ahead of his nearest challengers. Catlin, who won the Asian Tour Order of Merit in 2024, hit a six-under 64 in the fourth round to finish 20-under, earning his seventh title on the tour. Samooja led Cheung by a stroke going into the tricky 18th hole, but hit a bogey and had to settle for a joint second-place finish, as the latter secured the best finish for a Hong Kong player at the tournament in Fanling. "It's very, very special. Any time you can be on a trophy with some of the greatest players that ever played the game, I just feel very humble and very grateful," said Catlin. The 35-year-old was jointly leading the scoreboard along with Thomas Pieters and Caleb Surratt after the third round, where Cheung slipped from the top with three bogeys on Saturday. A clinical Catlin shook off a bogey on the fifth hole to take a solo lead on Sunday, and quickly fixed a mistake on the 14th as he found the centre of the green with a precise 120-yard stroke from thick grass to stay on course for a birdie. Error-prone Pieters and Surratt finished tied for sixth place with Sampson Zheng. Catlin's first trophy on the Asian Tour since April 2024 also earned him an invitation to next year's Open Championship and a maiden qualification for the Masters. "It's like a dream come true... it's been a long time coming, lot of hard work, lot of times when you weren't sure what was coming but you just kind of held the faith and I just kept working," Catlin said, shaking his head. "To finally be at the Masters, speechless."

item.title: Brookfield builds Qatar presence with Doha office
item.description: Alternative asset manager Brookfield said on Sunday it had opened an office in Doha anchored by its global credit platform as it deepens its presence in Qatar and expands across the Gulf region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alternative asset manager Brookfield (BAM.N) said on Sunday it had opened an office in Doha anchored by its global credit platform as it deepens its presence in Qatar and expands across the Gulf region. The Doha office will be anchored by Brookfield's global credit platform, including Oaktree, underscoring the growing role of private credit in financing Gulf economies The move deepens Brookfield's exposure to Qatar, including a $20 billion AI infrastructure investment programme with a QIA-backed AI company [USN:L4N3XF0P6 TEXT:"Qai"] Establishing a local presence gives Brookfield closer access to sovereign wealth funds, institutional investors and deal opportunities in what has been one of the region's fastest-growing investment markets Brookfield is the latest global investment firm to establish a presence in Qatar as asset managers expand local teams to capture investment opportunities across the Gulf One of the world's largest LNG exporters before the war, Qatar is trying to diversify its economy away from energy and attract foreign investment

item.title: NHL roundup: Leafs erupt in third, rout Oilers for fourth straight win
item.description: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday. Jack Roslovic recorded a goal and an assist, while Auston Matthews, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored and Kirill Marchenko nabbed two assists. For Edmonton, Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard had two helpers each. Anthony Stolarz stopped 30 shots for his fourth victory as Toronto posted its first four-game win streak since January. Tristan Jarry turned away 25 shots for the Oilers, who had won three in a row. With his 11th and 12th goals of the season, Draisaitl shares the NHL lead with the Minnesota Wild's Kirill Kaprizov. Draisaitl is second in the league in scoring with 23 points -- 10 shy of McDavid, who has eight goals and a league-leading 25 assists. Mammoth 5, Lightning 4 (OT) Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting Utah past Tampa Bay in Salt Lake City. Simashev slipped in a pass from Barrett Hayton at 1:44 for his first career game-winner. Utah also received goals from Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther and Anders Lee. Vincent Trocheck had two assists. Mammoth goaltender Karel Vejmelka made 29 saves and earned the secondary assist on Simashev's winner. Jake Guentzel, Pontus Holmberg, Brayden Point and Conor Geekie hit the net for the Lightning, and Dennis Hildeby made 23 saves. Nikita Kucherov collected an assist for his 1,138th career point, passing Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead. Blue Jackets 2, Golden Knights 1 (OT) Adam Fantilli scored a power-play goal 59 seconds into overtime to lead Columbus to a victory over visiting Vegas. It was Fantilli's third goal of the season and snapped a 0-for-22 drought on the power play for the Blue Jackets. Denton Mateychuk also scored a goal, Kent Johnson added two assists and Cam Talbot finished with 26 saves. Tomas Hertl scored for Vegas and Hart stopped 18 of 20 shots for Vegas, which saw its losing streak extended to a season-high three games. The Golden Knights have allowed a power-play goal in five straight games. Penguins 3, Predators 2 (OT) Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for ailing Pittsburgh, which rallied to take down visiting Nashville. Connor Dewar and Rickard Rakell also scored for the Penguins, who won their second straight game. Arturs Silovs finished with 24 saves, marking the first time the team has won consecutive games since starting the season 2-0. Steven Stamkos scored his fifth of the season and Jayden Struble notched his first for the Predators, who are 0-4 in overtime and shootouts. Juuse Saros made a season-high 34 saves, but Rakell spoiled his bid for a victory by tying the game with 1:06 remaining in regulation. Bruins 6, Sharks 4 Boston scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, to edge visiting San Jose and run its unbeaten streak to eight games. David Pastrnak tied former teammate Patrice Bergeron for third on Boston's all-time goals list (427) to kick off the late-game surge. Fraser Minten (game-winner), James Hagens and Casey Mittelstadt all had a goal and an assist, while Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka each dished out two assists, and Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves. Michael Misa, Kiefer Sherwood, Dmitry Orlov and Will Smith each scored a goal, Jacob Trouba had two assists, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 shots for the Sharks, who were on a two-game win streak. Ducks 5, Flyers 4 Tristan Luneau had a goal and two assists as visiting Anaheim snapped a five-game losing streak with a victory over Philadelphia. Leo Carlsson chipped in with a goal and an assist against the team that signed him to a five-year, $90 million offer sheet over the summer. Anaheim ultimately matched the deal, making the 21-year-old the highest paid player in the league. Beckett Sennecke and A.J. Greer also scored and Lukas Dostal turned aside 28 shots. Matvei Michkov scored his seventh and eighth goals for Philadelphia, which had won three straight since losing its first nine. Porter Martone had a goal and an assist and Tyson Foerster also scored, while Trevor Zegras recorded two assists against his former team. Joseph Woll finished with 21 saves. Devils 3, Kings 1 Arseny Gritsyuk scored for the fifth straight game to help New Jersey seal a win against Los Angeles in Newark, N.J. Anthony Mantha and Brett Pesce also scored, and Jake Allen made 12 saves for New Jersey, which has won three straight and five of the past six. Scott Laughton scored and Anton Forsberg made 23 saves for the Kings, who had won two in a row following a 0-4-2 start to the season. Senators 7, Rangers 4 Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as Ottawa topped visiting New York. Jake Sanderson tallied one goal and added two assists, while Dylan Cozens and Michael Amadio each scored and chipped in a helper. Tim Stutzle also found the back of the net as Ottawa improved to 5-2-0 on home ice. Jonas Johansson, making his Senators and season debut, made 24 saves. J.T. Miller and Will Cuylle each scored and added an assist, and Alexis Lafreniere and Pavel Dorofeyev also scored for the Rangers, who are 1-3-1 in their last five. Adam Fox and Noah Laba each added a pair of helpers, and Dylan Garand stopped 17 shots. Hurricanes 4, Blues 0 Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves to lead Carolina to a road victory over St. Louis. Sean Walker, Jesperi Kotkaniemi, Logan Stankoven, and Nikolaj Ehlers all lit the lamp as the Hurricanes closed out their five-game road trip with a victory and a 3-2-0 record. Sebastian Aho and Seth Jarvis each picked up a pair of assists, while Joel Hofer finished with 35 saves in the losing effort. Wild 5, Kraken 1 Kirill Kaprizov scored his 12th goal of the season -- tying for the league lead -- and added an assist as Minnesota dominated host Seattle. Kaprizov, who is tied for first in goals with the Edmonton Oilers' Leon Draisaitl, opened the scoring on a breakaway just 26 seconds into the game. Blake Coleman scored twice, including an empty-netter with 3:36 remaining, while Joel Eriksson Ek added a goal and an assist and Olli Maatta also tallied. Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves. Berkly Catton scored for the Kraken, who had won their previous two games. Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 shots. Capitals 4, Sabres 3 Alex Tuch scored his second goal of the game at 3:42 of overtime to lift host Washington to victory over Buffalo, his former team. Tuch, acquired by Washington in a sign-and-trade deal with Buffalo in June, was in the slot to take a pass from Dylan Strome behind the net and beat a screened Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen inside the left post. Strome also scored twice, and Charlie Lindgren made 18 saves for the Capitals. Jack Quinn, Josh Doan and Noah Ostlund scored for the Sabres, who built a 2-0 lead halfway through the first period. Luukkonen made 30 saves. Flames 4, Red Wings 1 Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as Calgary cruised past visiting Detroit, snapping the Red Wings' eight-game winning streak in the series. Matvei Gridin had a goal and an assist for the Flames, while Ryan Strome and Zayne Parekh also scored. Matt Coronato added two assists. Devin Cooley made 28 saves for Calgary, which has won three straight and four of their last five games after opening the season with five consecutive losses. Andrew Copp scored the lone goal for Detroit, which had won three of its previous four games. John Gibson made 21 saves after leaving his previous start Thursday because of an eye issue. --Field Level Media

item.title: Audi to invest $4.2 billion in first US factory, plans to build 2 lakh SUVs annually
item.description: Audi plans to invest $4.2 billion in its first US factory in Georgia, targeting annual production of 2 lakh SUVs and creating around 4,500 jobs. Construction is expected to begin in 2027, with production scheduled to start in the early 2030s.
item.dc:creator: Pragya Singha Roy
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday, October 24, 2026, that German luxury carmaker Audi plans to invest $4.2 billion (around ₹37,000 crore) in a new vehicle assembly plant near Macon, Georgia. It is Audi's first car manufacturing plant in the United States and will be able to make 200,000 SUVs a year and about 4,500 jobs.The announcement came ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, as Trump continues to promote his tariff policies as a way to boost domestic manufacturing. Audi, a subsidiary of Volkswagen Group, confirmed the investment in a statement, stating construction will start in 2027 and production in the early 2030s. The investment comes in the wake of a growing push by foreign car makers to ramp up production in the U.S., Reuters reported.Audi to manufacture premium SUVs in GeorgiaAudi is planning to make some of the biggest SUVs at the proposed plant in Georgia. According to a US official cited by Reuters, the plant is expected to assemble the Audi Q7, Q8 and Q9 models. At the event Audi CEO Gernot Döllner said that the company plans to make its biggest and most expensive SUVs locally, indicating its plans to have a long-term presence in the American market.According to Audi, the investment will help the company consolidate its role as a strong production base in North America, in addition to Europe and China. At present, the company imports all the vehicles sold in the US from Europe or Mexico. Last year, the US tariffs cost Audi some €1.2 billion (around $1.4 billion), according to Reuters.Trump credits tariffs for Audi's investmentTrump made the announcement of the proposed factory at a campaign rally in Perry, near Macon, Georgia, on Saturday. He touted the investment as proof that his trade policies were promoting automakers to move to the US.Republican Senator Bernie Moreno also attributed tariffs and regulations for the proposed plant. However, critics argue that higher import duties have increased vehicle prices and created uncertainty around investment decisions. The announcement comes as Democrats push the economy, such as the effects of tariff policy, as a topic in battleground midterm elections.Volkswagen faces global challengesInvestment follows as Volkswagen Group is under pressure from Chinese competition, falling demand in Europe and trade barriers in the US. Reuters reports that sales of Audis are down 7% worldwide in the first half of 2026 and 16% in the U.S.Other car companies are also looking to increase US production. Toyota announced a $3.6 billion investment in a Texas truck assembly facility in July 2026, with completion targeted by 2030 and around 2,000 jobs expected. At the same time, Honda expressed worries about the uncertainty of trade policy, and Hyundai has tied additional U.S. investment in Mexico and Canada with greater clarity on the future of the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement.Audi's proposed Georgia plant would be a significant change in the South's production strategy, but it is expected to start rolling off the manufacturing line in the early 2030s.

item.title: Russie-Trois morts dans des attaques dans la région de Belgorod
item.description: Deux personnes ont été tuées et 13 autres blessées dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche par une attaque de drone ukrainienne contre la ville de Belgorod, en Russie, près de la frontière entre les deux pays, ont déclaré les autorités locales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deux personnes ont été tuées et 13 autres blessées dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche par une attaque de drone ukrainienne contre la ville de Belgorod, en Russie, près de la frontière entre les deux pays, ont déclaré les autorités locales. "L'attaque a endommagé 30 ensembles d'appartements, 35 voitures, quatre maisons, trois bâtiments administratifs, huit locaux commerciaux et trois installations sociales", a dit le gouverneur de la région de Belgorod, Alexandre Chouvaïev. Une troisième personne a été tuée et une autre blessée dans un village près de la ville de Chebekino, ont dit les autorités.

item.title: Russia says it hit a cargo vessel and Ukrainian logistic hubs overnight
item.description: The Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk during an overnight attack.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk during an overnight attack. The ministry said the vessel was being used to supply the Ukrainian army. Russian forces also hit a logistics centre, a distribution centre and a logistics terminal in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv. The ministry said the facilities had been used for storage and distribution of dual-use cargo for the Ukrainian military. Reuters could not independently verify the Defence Ministry's information.

item.title: Three people killed and 14 injured in Ukrainian attacks on Russia's Belgorod region, governor says
item.description: An overnight Ukrainian drone attack on the city of Belgorod near the Russian border with Ukraine killed two people and injured 13, local authorities said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An overnight Ukrainian drone attack on the city of Belgorod near the Russian border with Ukraine killed two people and injured 13, local authorities said on Sunday. "The attack has damaged 30 blocks of flats, 35 cars, four houses, three administrative buildings, eight commercial premises and three social facilities," said Belgorod regional governor Alexander Shuvayev. Another person was killed and one was injured in a village near the town of Shebekino, authorities said.

item.title: バルセロナで「反体制」暴徒が略奪・放火、ブリュッセルでは警察と衝突 - Reuters
item.description: バルセロナで「反体制」暴徒が略奪・放火、ブリュッセルでは警察と衝突 Reuters

item.title: バルセロナで「反体制」暴徒が略奪・放火、ブリュッセルでは警察と衝突
item.description: [バルセロナ／ブリュッセル ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[バルセロナ／ブリュッセル ２４日 ロイター] - スペインのバルセロナで２４日夜、反体制を掲げた抗議活動の一部参加者が市中心部で店舗を略奪、路上の公共設備に放火するなど暴徒化し、約１００人が拘束された。抗議活動はソーシャルメディア（ＳＮＳ）で呼びかけられ、多くの若者が参加していた。ベルギーの首都ブリュッセルでも同日、反政府デモ隊と警察が衝突するなど、各地で混乱が続いている。

現場となったバルセロナのカタルーニャ広場は観光客や地元の買い物客でにぎわう市内有数の人気スポットで、カタルーニャ自治州の当局によると周辺の１４店舗が被害を受け、放火も３０件以上あった。拘束された人の約４分の１は未成年だという。ＳＮＳに投稿された動画には、フードを被った黒ずくめの一群が店の窓ガラスを蹴破り商品を奪って逃走する様子が映っており、一部ではオンラインの視聴者が破壊・略奪行為をあおる場面もみられた。

今回のデモは、ＳＮＳ上で「体制に反対する」運動への参加を呼びかける形で広まった。フランスで抗議活動を展開してきた学生たちを動員するために使われた「憤慨する高校生たち」というキャッチフレーズも掲げられていた。

若者を中心に数百人が抗議活動に参加したブリュッセルでは、警察に追われて転倒したデモ参加者を警察官が暴行する場面や、デモ隊が自転車や道路標識などを積み上げて火を放とうとする場面をロイター記者が目撃。別の場所では、警察が催涙ガスを使ったとの現地報道もあった。ただ、前の週に起きた衝突ほど大規模化せず、地元警察は大きな事件は発生しなかったと発表した。

item.title: Britain's migration clampdown puts fear into $20 billion care sector
item.description: Roughly one-third of workers in the UK's wider adult care sector are migrants, according to the Work Rights Centre ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Lucy White In Britain, the government ensures that more than 650,000 vulnerable people receive daily visits from carers who help them wash, eat and attend to any medical conditions. That same government’s crackdown on immigration is putting the sector at risk. Roughly one-third of workers in the UK’s wider adult care sector are migrants, according to the Work Rights Centre. Around 280,000 came to the country under a Health and Care Visa between February 2022 and July 2025, a route that has since been suspended by the Labour government over fears it was being abused. Holders of the visas brought with them 429,200 dependents, many of whom also ended up working in the care sector. At the time the visa was suspended, Labour — under then-prime minister Keir Starmer — lagged far behind Nigel Farage’s far-right Reform UK in voter surveys. With migration high on voters’ concerns, the ruling party in September 2025 tasked a new home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, with introducing even greater restrictions on new arrivals as well as non-citizens already working in the UK. The government has signaled that, from July 2028, migrants will no longer be able to renew their Health and Care Visa, and instead will have to transfer to a Skilled Worker route. That carries a much higher salary requirement, and domiciliary care businesses — many of whom rely on contracts from local authorities — say they don’t get enough funding to cover paychecks of that scale.  “I will have to either downsize or just sell to a corporation,” said Shweta Maulayah, a managing director of a small care business called Maucare. “This is something that I built with passion, but I would not be able to financially keep it afloat.” The 2028 date looms large for many businesses and workers in the domiciliary care and supported living sector, which combined is worth around £15 billion ($20 billion), and their jitters are being heightened by Mahmood’s so-called “earned settlement” proposals.  Under current rules, a person arriving in Britain must stay for five years before they can apply for settlement, meaning most carers who came in 2022 and early 2023 would be eligible by the time the Health and Care Visa expires. But now Mahmood is proposing that the five-year baseline should be extended to 10 years, with reductions for high earners and those who make exceptional contributions to society through volunteering. Maulayah started recruiting from abroad in January 2023, and so has several staff who wouldn’t be eligible for settlement under those terms before the July 2028 visa deadline. “How am I going to keep them if it goes to 10 years?” she asked.Labour PoliticsPrime Minister Andy Burnham is leaning toward excluding care workers from the extension, according to a report in the Times newspaper, though it’s unclear whether the Home Office would support exemptions for people with Health and Care Visas.  Some Labour backbenchers object to the application of the new rules to people already in the country. Bloomberg reported in March that more than 100 parliamentarians signed a private letter urging the home secretary to rethink her plans. Left-leaning Labour lawmakers have made a set of demands, according to one person familiar with the matter, including that the new timelines for settlement shouldn’t be applied retroactively, that people from the same household should be able to benefit from the same timeline, and that the maximum timeline to claim settled status should be seven years. Cabinet ministers including Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh and Housing Secretary Angela Rayner have also refused to publicly back Mahmood’s reforms. Mike Tapp, a former Home Office minister who worked with Mahmood on the proposals, has also called for an exemption for care workers. During Labour’s annual conference last month the home secretary gave a first hint that she was rethinking aspects of her reforms. “I know that, throughout our consultation process, some have said elements of these reforms are not fair,” she said. “We will come to a position that balances fairness for those who came here legally and fairness to British citizens across this country.” But that might come too late for some care firms. One owner of a domiciliary care business in the south of England, who was granted anonymity discussing commercial matters, said the uncertainty has prompted her to explore options to sell her firm or wind it up. Even if exemptions from Mahmood’s reforms were introduced for care workers, she worried that current restrictions on hiring workers from abroad ultimately made her business unsustainable, as she’d find it hard to hire British staff willing to work at the pay levels her contracts with the local authority allow. Maulayah faces the same dilemma. “We’re not getting a lot of locals joining this industry,” she said. “Even youngsters that go to career fairs, they’re not that interested because they feel that care is a low-skilled job. One of them said to me, ‘I’d rather stack shelves in Tesco,’” she said, referring to the Tesco Plc supermarket chain. Back in 2022, the industry was crying out for more staff. Thousands of workers from European Union countries had left the UK following Brexit, while its aging population meant there was relentless demand.  But, following an influx from countries such as India and Nigeria, it emerged that unscrupulous care agencies were abusing the sponsored visa route. A Bloomberg investigation last year revealed that many carers who entered the UK to work in good faith were being charged tens of thousands of pounds for their visa by the business who was supposed to be sponsoring them, but that there was no job for them when they arrived in the country.  Speaking to journalists on Friday, Burnham stopped short of committing to all of Mahmood’s proposals. “We’ve been consulting on those reforms, and we will come forward with our decisions soon,” the PM said. “But I strongly support the Home Secretary when she says that settlement is a right to be earned through contribution.” Proposals are expected next month. A spokesperson for the Home Office didn’t respond to requests from Bloomberg for comment.

item.title: Most Gulf shares close lower as Saudi-Houthi fighting rages on
item.description: Most Gulf bourses ended lower on Sunday and Saudi Arabia's index registered its worst session in 18 months as fighting between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis showed no sign of abating.
item.dc:creator: Ateeq Shariff
item.content:encoded: Most Gulf bourses ended lower on Sunday and Saudi Arabia's index registered its worst session in 18 months as fighting between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis showed no sign of abating. Saudi air defences downed drones and missiles over Riyadh and the south on Sunday, [USN:L2N46A05D TEXT:"the Saudi-led coalition said"]. A day earlier, the Houthis said they [USN:L2N46A00K TEXT:"hit Saudi oil facilities and airports"] and the Saudi-led coalition said it downed two missiles. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) pared losses to finish 2.7% lower after falling as much as 3.4%. The index posted its worst intraday performance since April 2025, with heavyweight Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) falling 0.9%. GCC stocks stayed under pressure as tensions and shipping disruptions in key waterways kept investors wary. Fears of renewed US military action dented de-escalation hopes, with traders awaiting diplomatic progress, said George Pavel, general manager at Naga.com Middle East. In Qatar, the index (.QSI) reversed early losses to inch 0.1% higher. Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) plunged 3.6%, its biggest single-day fall since June 2025, with most of its constituents in negative territory. Saudi Arabia (.TASI) declined 2.7% to 9,439 Qatar (.QSI) inched 0.1% higher to 8,615 Egypt (.EGX30) dropped 3.6% to 49,234 Bahrain (.BAX) eased 0.2% to 1,849 Oman (.MSX30) retreated 1.4% to 7,278 Kuwait (.BKP) added 0.5% to 8,768

item.title: NBA roundup: Nikola Jokic records 199th triple-double, Nuggets top Pels
item.description: Nikola Jokic recorded 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, Jamal Murray poured in 42 points and the Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to top the visiting New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nikola Jokic recorded 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, Jamal Murray poured in 42 points and the Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to top the visiting New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night. Jokic has 199 career regular-season triple-doubles in 12 seasons, second to just-retired Russell Westbrook's 209 in 18 seasons starting in 2008-09. Trevon Brazile scored seven of his 17 points in overtime and hit a corner 3-pointer late in the extra period, Christian Braun had 15 points in the game and DeMar DeRozan added 12 points for the Nuggets. Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22, Zion Williamson and Derik Queen contributed 17 each, Saddiq Bey scored 14 and Jeremiah Fears added 10. Hornets 115, Heat 110 Brandon Miller pumped in 34 points and Charlotte recovered from blowing a 23-point lead to beat visiting Miami. Dennis Schroder added 25 points, Naz Reid scored 23 and Grayson Allen contributed 20. Miller was the only one of the Hornets' top four scorers who played for the team last season. Davion Mitchell's 22 points and 10 assists paced the Heat, who remained winless through three games despite erasing a 23-point deficit to tie the score at 100. Bam Adebayo's 20 points and eight rebounds gave Miami a lift, Pelle Larsson supplied 15 points, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson each had 14, and Bobby Portis scored 13. Cavaliers 125, Nets 121 Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as Cleveland built a 22-point lead before holding on for a victory over visiting Brooklyn. Evan Mobley added 20 points and 10 rebounds, and Jaylon Tyson scored 15 points off the bench in the Cavaliers' home opener. James Harden collected 12 points, eight rebounds and seven assists as Cleveland picked up its first win. Brooklyn, which trailed 104-82 with 9:29 remaining, pulled within 123-121 on Michael Porter Jr.'s 3-pointer with 8.1 seconds left. Porter (28 points, nine rebounds) fouled out on the subsequent possession and Sam Merrill hit two free throws to put the Cavaliers up four with 5.2 seconds remaining. Julius Randle had 23 points for winless Brooklyn. 76ers 127, Bucks 116 Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead Philadelphia to a home win over Milwaukee. Embiid finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for the 76ers, who rested LeBron James (back/sciatica). James is expected to play Sunday against the Detroit Pistons, while Embiid will rest in the second half of a back-to-back. Tyrese Maxey pitched in with 26 points, while VJ Edgecombe delivered a 17-point, 13-rebound effort. While Philadelphia is 3-0 on the young season, the Bucks fell to 0-3 despite eight players scoring in double figures. Jaime Jaquez Jr. led Milwaukee with 21 points, while Kel'el Ware had 19 points and 13 rebounds off the bench for the visitors. Wizards 124, Bulls 120 Trae Young paired 25 points with nine assists and Kyshawn George added 22 points and nine rebounds as Washington downed host Chicago to open a three-game road trip. The Wizards outscored the Bulls 40-20 in the third quarter. Anthony Davis and Young combined to go 6-for-6 from the free-throw line to hold onto the lead. Davis (19 points) and Tre Johnson (13) also scored in double figures for Washington, while Justin Champagnie had an 11-point, 14-rebound double-double. Chicago rookie Caleb Wilson contributed 30 points and 14 rebounds for his first career double-double, and teammate Matas Buzelis scored 21 points. Norman Powell added 18, Jalen Smith had 14 and Tre Jones 10. Josh Giddey had nine points, 10 assists and eight rebounds. Suns 131, Warriors 122 Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds and host Phoenix won to send Golden State to its worst start in almost two decades. Miles Bridges scored 16 points and Dillon Brooks added 15 points for the Suns, who won their home opener. Booker set a franchise record for points in a home opener. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 26 points and nine rebounds and De'Anthony Melton scored 25 points for the Warriors, who fell to 0-3 for the first time since 2007-08. Golden State was without starters Stephen Curry (knee), Brandin Podziemski (back) and Draymond Green (back) and reserve Al Horford (back). Spurs 122, Mavericks 106 Victor Wembanyama scored 23 points as visiting San Antonio earned its first win of the season by defeating short-handed Dallas in the second of a back-to-back for both teams. Dylan Harper added 22 points, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle scored 19 each, Julian Champagnie hit for 12 off the bench and Devin Vassell tallied 11 points for the Spurs. Wembanyama also posted seven rebounds and four blocks. The Mavericks played without stars Cooper Flagg (shoulder) and Kyrie Irving, who was held out for left knee injury management. Flagg sprained his left shoulder in a win at Indiana on Friday and will be reevaluated next week. Rookie Sergio De Larrea's 21 points led Dallas. Marcus Sasser, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford scored 12 apiece. Rockets 121, Hawks 114 Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as Houston topped host Atlanta to improve to 3-0. The Rockets also got 19 points apiece from Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard, who started in place of Fred VanVleet (right knee load management). Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each scored 17 points, with Sengun grabbing 10 rebounds and Thompson collecting 11. The Hawks were led by Jalen Johnson, who fell just shy of a triple-double with 26 points, 16 assists and nine rebounds. Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels scored 18 points apiece, and CJ McCollum added 17. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brazil votes in tight runoff between leftist Lula and Bolsonaro Jr.
item.description: Corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling dominated the race.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin
item.content:encoded: Brazilians voted on Sunday in a tight runoff vote that could shift Latin America's largest nation sharply rightward, bringing it closer to the United States as part of a broader conservative shift across the region. The runoff pits leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro. Flavio scored [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"a major upset at the start of the month"] by defying pollsters to lead voting in the first round. A victory for Bolsonaro, 45, would extend a wave of right-wing victories for Latin American candidates friendly to US President Donald Trump while a fourth mandate for Lula would be a disappointment in Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security. Reuters on Saturday [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"revealed a campaign"] within Trump's State Department to help get the Bolsonaros back in power. Brazil's election race has been dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling, which Washington denies. It has also been colored by fallout from [USN:L1N43T0Q4 TEXT:"Jair Bolsonaro's 2025"] conviction for plotting a 2022 coup, with Flavio pledging to free his father if elected. Trump has called the case a "witch hunt" and imposed a 50% tariff on Brazil in 2025, in a decision explicitly linked to Jair Bolsonaro’s trial. While this was later watered down, Trump unleashed [USN:L1N43P1HE TEXT:"new levies against Brazil this year"], citing unfair trade practices. Lula has cast the Trump administration’s proximity to the Bolsonaro clan as part of an attempt to sway the election, while labeling tariffs and other punitive measures as bullying. On economic issues, despite falling inequality and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over an electorate grappling with high living costs and heavy household debt. Endemic gang violence also weighs on voters’ minds. Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns and has promised a heavy-handed approach to fighting crime, pledging maximum-security jails and chemical castration for serious sexual offenses. Casting his ballot in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday, Flavio Bolsonaro urged people to come out vote "come rain or shine". Lula, meanwhile, is due to vote in São Bernardo do Campo, near Sao Paulo. CANDIDATES ARE NECK AND NECK Polls show the candidates are practically tied going into the runoff. Historical precedent favors Bolsonaro, however, as no candidate has ever won the presidency after coming second in the first-round vote. Bolsonaro picked up 47% of ballots cast in the first round, while Lula trailed with 45%. The senator's first-round win [USN:L6N45Q08A TEXT:"sent Brazil's markets and currency soaring"] on expectations of pro-business reforms. His first-round success was mirrored in congressional elections for his Liberal Party and other right-wing politicians, which could pave a legislative path for him, or complicate governance for Lula.

item.title: Disenchanted Netanyahu supporters are prize of Israel election campaign
item.description: Labor has dwindled to a rump as Israeli politics have shifted rightwards, and there are now around half a dozen other parties courting Likud voters, from the center to the far right.
item.dc:creator: Emily Rose, Maayan Lubell
item.content:encoded: In the remote Negev Desert town of Dimona, long a bastion of Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party, disenchanted voters are going door-to-door campaigning for his top rival, hoping to bring down the veteran prime minister in Israel's election on Tuesday. The ballot is Israel's first since Hamas' October 7, 2023, surprise attack that shook the country and plunged the region into turmoil, as Israel went to war on the militant group in Gaza and its allies in Lebanon and Iran. The October 7 security breach saw Likud's popularity plummet. Opinion polls for months have predicted Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties losing its majority. But his top rival, centrist Gadi Eisenkot, has no clear path to power either, and the race has become tighter as the election nears. Dimona, where an Iranian missile wounded dozens in March, has become a political battleground. "We must have change. Bibi has to go," said Yossi Assayag, 74, who says he has supported Likud most his life. "Bibi has brought disaster to Israel." LIKUD LOYALISTS Assayag is part of a cohort of town residents trying to convince their community to vote for Eisenkot's party Yashar, which is neck-and-neck with Likud in the polls. It's a tough task in Dimona, where half the voters in the previous 2022 election cast a ballot for Likud. "I will never betray Likud," said Ruti Ohana, a pensioner, who says she has voted Likud ever since immigrating to Israel from North Africa more than 60 years ago. She said Netanyahu was a cut above his rivals, and the blame he receives from detractors for October 7 was unfair. Right-wing Likud long ago formed a core voter base among Jews of Middle Eastern and North African descent, known as Mizrahis, who felt neglected by the European-influenced centre-left Labor Party that dominated Israel for generations. Labor has since dwindled to a rump as Israeli politics have shifted rightwards, and there are now around half a dozen other parties courting Likud voters, from the centre to the far right. But the link to the party among its past supporters remains strong. "Most people here vote for Likud just because that's how they were raised," said Oria Asaf, 25, a past Likud voter now backing Yashar. "The change will come when people start to think about their children's future rather than their parents' past." BATTLE FOR WAVERING LIKUDNIKS While Netanyahu has a hard core of supporters that can't be won over, the prize is undecided voters who "understand that we are in a state of crisis" and are open to persuasion, said Michal Elmalem Abu, elected as a member of the city council from Likud and now leading Eisenkot's Dimona campaign. Some 13% of Israeli voters have yet to decide how they will vote, according to data collected by the Viterbi Family Center for Public Opinion and Policy Research at the Israel Democracy Institute. Of those who voted for Likud in 2022, just 55% now say they will vote for the party again on Tuesday. Fifteen percent will support parties aligned against Netanyahu, including 8% for Yashar. Another 14% will vote for alternative right-wing parties, and 9% are undecided. It is in places just like Dimona where Eisenkot stands a chance to bite a chunk out of Likud's base, said Amotz Asa-El, a political scientist at the Hartman Institute. A child of Moroccan immigrants who rose through the ranks to become military chief of staff, Eisenkot, 66, has a personal story of humble origins from the Mizrahi community that "appeals to a big swath of the Israeli electorate, particularly Likud's traditional electorate", said Asa-El. In an electoral field crowded with ex-soldiers, his peerless security credentials are an asset. The loss of his son, killed in combat in Gaza in December 2023, resonates with voters. At a town hall during a visit to Dimona in July, residents said they were excited about the prospect of a leader of Mizrahi descent. Others approached him with hugs and tearful condolences for the loss of his son. But a week later Netanyahu held his own event, demonstrating his powerful appeal in the hardscrabble Negev, where Likud governments have long boasted of bringing development funds. "Look around you, look at your community, look at what was here then and what is here now, and ask yourselves which governments invested in this monumental effort. And I do this out of immense love," he said. Lior Katzav, a Likud former mayor of Kiryat Malachi, another small-town stronghold, said party surveys show voters who had abandoned Likud are returning as the election nears. But even some who are sympathetic to Netanyahu say it may be time for a change. Israel's youngest prime minister when he was first elected 30 years ago, he has since become its longest-serving, now 77, having governed for 18 years over six terms. "It's time for him to go," said Dimona software engineer David Iskali. "He's done a lot for Israel but it can't go on. I won't give my vote to someone almost 80-years-old."

item.title: World Series rematch, Indian edition: Yankees beat Dodgers in Mumbai event
item.description: Mumbai's cricket fans packed the stands at the Andheri Sports Complex on Saturday to watch Indian World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav swing a bat - just not the kind that they are used to.
item.dc:creator: Revathi Hariharan
item.content:encoded: Mumbai's cricket fans packed the stands at the Andheri Sports Complex on Saturday to watch Indian World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav swing a bat - just not the kind that they are used to. Indian cricketers Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Deepak Chahar and Radha Yadav lined up alongside ex-Major League Baseball players Nick Swisher, Adrian Gonzalez, Jake Arrieta and Jonny Gomes in a three-on-three tournament that organisers pitched as a bridge between the two bat-and-ball games. Each of the four teams mixed a baseball veteran, an Indian cricketer and an American softball player and the scoring rewarded both muscle and precision. A home run earned two points, hitting the target zone earned four and fielders picked up one point for a catch, while five consecutive out-of-the-park hits doubled a team's total. The semifinals offered up both a thriller and a stroll, as Gonzalez's Los Angeles Dodgers overturned the Shardul-led Chicago Cubs' 44 runs with just a minute to spare, while Suryakumar's New York Yankees cruised past the Boston Red Sox. That set up a rematch of the 2024 World Series, this time in India, with the Yankees posting 78 and holding off the Dodgers to be crowned champions. Softball player Rachel Garcia was named the tournament's most valuable player. Suryakumar, a former India captain who guided the side to victory at this year's Twenty20 Cricket World Cup on home soil, said he is confident baseball will grow in India and that cricketing skills can translate to success in the American sport. "I think it's all about good range hitting," added Suryakumar, whose celebrations spilled into the stands as he placed the gold chain he won around his wife's neck after the win. "You must be strong from head to your lower body, have a good core and strong arms. If you want to hit 450 feet, 500 feet, you got to be strong. Work hard. No substitutes."

Rachel Garcia, representing the New York Yankees, in action during MLBx Mumbai, Major League Baseball's fast-paced 3-on-3 baseball event, in Mumbai, India, October 24, 2026. REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas

Former New York Yankees player Nick Swisher, Indian cricketer Suryakumar Yadav and American softball player Rachel Garcia celebrate after winning the tournament during MLBx Mumbai, Major League Baseball's fast-paced 3-on-3 baseball event, in Mumbai, India, October 24, 2026. REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas

FAST

MUMBAI, Oct 25 : Mumbai's cricket fans packed the stands at the Andheri Sports Complex on Saturday to watch Indian World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav swing a bat - just not the kind that they are used to. Indian cricketers Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Deepak Chahar and Radha Yadav lined up alongside ex-Major League Baseball players Nick Swisher, Adrian Gonzalez, Jake Arrieta and Jonny Gomes in a three-on-three tournament that organisers pitched as a bridge between the two bat-and-ball games. Each of the four teams mixed a baseball veteran, an Indian cricketer and an American softball player and the scoring rewarded both muscle and precision. A home run earned two points, hitting the target zone earned four and fielders picked up one point for a catch, while five consecutive out-of-the-park hits doubled a team's total.

The semifinals offered up both a thriller and a stroll, as Gonzalez's Los Angeles Dodgers overturned the Shardul-led Chicago Cubs' 44 runs with just a minute to spare, while Suryakumar's New York Yankees cruised past the Boston Red Sox. That set up a rematch of the 2024 World Series, this time in India, with the Yankees posting 78 and holding off the Dodgers to be crowned champions. Softball player Rachel Garcia was named the tournament's most valuable player. Suryakumar, a former India captain who guided the side to victory at this year's Twenty20 Cricket World Cup on home soil, said he is confident baseball will grow in India and that cricketing skills can translate to success in the American sport. "I think it's all about good range hitting," added Suryakumar, whose celebrations spilled into the stands as he placed the gold chain he won around his wife's neck after the win. "You must be strong from head to your lower body, have a good core and strong arms. If you want to hit 450 feet, 500 feet, you got to be strong. Work hard. No substitutes."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Borr Drilling rig sinks off Gabon, one person dead and four missing
item.description: Borr Drilling's Prospector 5 drilling rig sank late on Saturday off the coast of Mayumba, Gabon, killing one worker and leaving four others missing among the 115 people on board, officials and the company said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Gnaneshwar Rajan, Colleen Goko
item.content:encoded: Borr Drilling's (BORR.N) Prospector 5 drilling rig sank late on Saturday off the coast of Mayumba, Gabon, killing one worker and leaving four others missing among the 115 people on board, officials and the company said on Sunday. One of the five initially unaccounted for, an Indian national, has been found dead, according to Sylvain Mayabi Binet, secretary general of the National Organization of Petroleum Employees. The remaining four missing people are three Gabonese nationals and one other expatriate. "Preliminary information indicates that the rig experienced a punch-through event during preload activities, resulting in loss of stability and the subsequent sinking of the rig," the offshore drilling contractor said. The Prospector 5 oil and gas rig, owned and operated by Borr, is contracted to support BW Energy's (BWE.OL) drilling operations off Gabon. The rig had not yet begun drilling. Prospector 5 is located at the Dussafu Marin permit, a licence off the Gabon coast. BW Energy holds a 73.5% working interest in the licence, with Panoro Energy holding 17.5%. Gabon's Ministry of Petroleum and Gas said it had activated a crisis unit and ordered the navy to reinforce search and rescue operations at sea. The ministry also ordered a technical investigation, Petroleum and Gas Minister Clotaire Kondja said in a statement. The crisis unit brings together the ministry, the navy, state oil company Gabon Oil, BW Energy and Borr Drilling, Kondja said. The accident occurred at approximately 9:40 p.m. (2040 GMT) on Saturday in the Dussafu Marin permit area near the Mabomont production facility, the ministry said. "We are deeply concerned for those who remain unaccounted for and everyone affected by this incident," said Borr Drilling Chief Executive Bruno Morand. "Our immediate priority is supporting the ongoing search and rescue efforts and the welfare of all personnel involved." Panoro Energy (PENR.OL) said production had been halted, adding that there were no reports of damage or accidental discharges. No discharge of harmful substances has been observed, the ministry said, adding that pollution-response resources remained deployed to protect the coastline and nearby Mayumba National Park.

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ブルワーズがＷＳで開幕2連勝、4点差からの逆転勝ち
item.description: ［ミルウォーキー ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ミルウォーキー　２４日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は２４日、ワールドシリーズ（ＷＳ、７回戦制）の第２戦を行い、ブルワーズが地元ウィスコンシン州ミルウォーキーでレイズに５─４で逆転勝ち。対戦成績を２勝０敗とした。

ブルワーズは一回表に４点を失ったが、その裏に４番ウィリアム・コントレラス捕手と６番ギャレット・ミッチェル中堅手の適時打で２点を返した。さらに、四回に相手のエラーで１点差に迫ると、六回に８番サル・フレリック右翼手が同点ソロ。続く七回に７番クーパー・プラット遊撃手のタイムリーで逆転した。

ブルワーズは小刻みな投手リレーで二回以降、無失点。５番手で登板し、１回１／３を無安打無失点に抑えたアブナー・ウリーベ投手が勝利投手となった。

第３戦は２６日、レイズの地元フロリダ州セントピーターズバーグで行われる。これまでにＷＳで０勝２敗から逆転優勝を果たしたのは１０チームのみで、１９９６年のヤンキースが最後。

item.title: サッカー＝ドルトムントが暫定首位に浮上、バイアーが決勝ゴール
item.description: ［ドルトムント（ドイツ） ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ドルトムント（ドイツ）　２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは２４日、各地で試合を行い、ドルトムントがアイントラハト・フランクフルトを１─０で下し、暫定ながら首位に浮上した。

なかなか得点が奪えず苦戦していたドルトムントだが、後半３５分にマクシミリアン・バイアーがペナルティーエリア手前から右足でネットを揺らし、これが決勝弾となった。フランクフルトの堂安律は先発し、後半４２分までプレー。同僚の小杉啓太はベンチ入りするも最後まで出場はなかった。

７試合を終えて無敗のドルトムントは勝ち点を１７に伸ばし、翌日に試合を控えるバイエルン・ミュンヘンに同３差をつけた。

佐野海舟が先発したマインツはブレーメンに２─３で黒星。佐野は後半アディショナルタイム１分までプレーした。チームメートの川崎颯太はベンチ外だった。田中聡がフル出場したシャルケはケルンとスコアドローで試合を終えた。

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝セブンティシクサーズ開幕3連勝、レブロンは欠場
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］　 -

米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は２４日、各地で試合を行い、セブンティシクサーズはバックスを１２７─１１６で下し、開幕から３連勝とした。

シクサーズのジョエル・エンビードが２８得点、１１リバウンド、１０アシストでキャリア通算１０回目のトリプルダブルを記録。ジェイレン・ブラウンが２７得点、タイリース・マクシーが２６得点で貢献した。シクサーズのレブロン・ジェームズは腰の痛みを考慮して、出場メンバーを外れた。

キャバリアーズはネッツを１２５─１２１で下し、スパーズはマーベリックスに１２２─１０６で快勝。いずれも今季初勝利を挙げた。ウィザーズはトレイ・ヤングが２５得点、４リバウンド、９アシストと活躍し、ブルズを１２４─１２０で退けた。

ロケッツはホークスを１２１─１１４で下し、３勝０敗に。ヒートはホーネッツに１１０─１１５で敗れ、開幕から３試合を終えて未勝利となった。

item.description: オバマ氏、中間選挙で「愚行に歯止め」と訴え トランプ政権を痛烈批判 Reuters

item.title: オバマ氏、中間選挙で「愚行に歯止め」と訴え トランプ政権を痛烈批判
item.description:
Dan Catchpole
[２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Dan Catchpole

[２４日 ロイター] - 米中間選挙が来週に迫り各地で応援合戦が熱を帯びる中、接戦の中西部２州で行われた民主党の集会にオバマ元大統領が登壇した。トランプ大統領本人や政権の対イラン政策などを痛烈に批判し、中間選挙での投票は現政権の「愚行を少しでも食い止める」ための「サーキットブレーカー」であり、ブレーカーを切り替えて政府に説明責任を求めるべきだと訴えた。

ミシガン州デトロイトで上院議員候補エルサイード氏の応援に立ったオバマ氏は、トランプ氏は国民の税金で私腹を肥やし利権を売り買いする前代未聞の大統領だとし、「今や共和党は腐敗した政府、無能な政府、機能しない政府の代名詞になってしまった」と批判した。米政権が「勝利」したとしている対イラン政策では、イランがホルムズ海峡を通過する船舶の攻撃を示唆することで石油輸出国を動揺させており、結果としてイランの影響力を高めることになったと指摘した。

さらに、政権の中枢部はさまつな事柄にしか興味がなく、ヘグセス国防長官を例に挙げ「兵士の顎のラインや男性ホルモンといった『重要問題』ばかり気にしている」と皮肉り、ホワイトハウスの改装についても悪趣味だとやゆした。

ホワイトハウスはコメントの求めに即座に応じなかった。ロイターとイプソスが８月に実施した世論調査では、トランプ一族が暗号資産関連で得た収益について６３％が不適切だと回答、「大統領の政策判断は私的なビジネス上の利害関係に影響されている」との回答は６９％に上っていた。

激戦州の一つとされるミシガン州では、ピーターズ民主党上院議員の引退に伴いエルサイード候補が共和党のロジャース元下院議員と接戦を繰り広げている。オバマ氏は民主党内で依然、最も人気の高い人物の１人で、デトロイトでの集会に先立ってオハイオ州クリーブランドでも、議席奪還を目指すブラウン元上院議員の応援演説を行なった。

item.title: Guadalajara gana de visita en el torneo mexicano de fútbol
item.description: Guadalajara, el club más popular del fútbol mexicano, ganó el sábado 1-0 de visita a Monterrey en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Guadalajara, el club más popular del fútbol mexicano, ganó el sábado 1-0 de visita a Monterrey en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura. Las "Chivas" de Guadalajara llegaron a 26 puntos para mantenerse en el segundo lugar general, por abajo del líder América que registra 27 unidades. En el partido, disputado en el estadio BBVA de Monterrey, Guadalajara anotó el gol del triunfo a los nueve minutos con un disparo cruzado de Roberto "Piojo" Alvarado tras recibir un pase de Santiago Sandoval, quien aprovechó un error defensivo de Víctor Guzmán para robar el balón. Monterrey tuvo la opción de empatar a los 19 minutos con un tiro penal, pero el portero Raúl Rangel atajó el disparo del argentino Lucas Ocampos. Los "Rayados" de Monterrey habían rescatado el empate en tiempo de reposición cuando el balón le rebotó en el pecho a Diego Rossi tras un desvío defensivo, pero el árbitro anuló el gol tras revisar en el VAR la jugada en la que el balón le pegó en la mano al centrocampista uruguayo. "Me gustó mucho el comportamiento del equipo en el aspecto defensivo y el orden que tuvimos para neutralizar a un equipo que cuenta con jugadores de mucho talento, con mucho desequilibrio y, además, muy bien trabajado. Me gustó el esfuerzo colectivo y la garra con la que se jugó el partido, es muy importante que mi equipo juegue con ese espíritu competitivo", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico de Guadalajara, el argentino Gabriel Milito. "Siempre digo que la contundencia es fundamental en el fútbol, encontrar el gol es determinante, pero también es muy importante generar situaciones, peor sería no generarlas, porque si no creas oportunidades es imposible marcar goles. El camino que queda por delante es duro, primero tenemos que terminar el torneo y después vendrá la Liguilla (Postemporada)", agregó. A la postemporada o liguilla clasifican los clubes que ocupan los primeros ocho lugares de la tabla general al final de las 17 jornadas de la temporada regular. En los otros partidos disputados el sábado, Pumas UNAM y Tigres UANL empataron 1-1 con goles del paraguayo Robert Morales y del argentino Juan Francisco Brunetta, respectivamente. León y Toluca empataron 1-1. Para León anotó José Alvarado, mientras que para los "Diablos Rojos" de Toluca lo hizo el uruguayo Federico Viñas. La jornada finalizará el domingo cuando Atlas sea local ante Puebla, el actual campeón Cruz Azul visite a Querétaro, América juegue ante Pachuca y Tijuana sea rival de Santos Laguna. El viernes, Atlético de San Luis ganó de visita al Atlante por 1-0. Por su parte, Necaxa y Bravos de Ciudad Juárez empataron 1-1.

item.title: Kawano, Henderson set world marathon race walk records
item.description: Japan's Masatora Kawano and Australia's Rebecca Henderson set the men's and women's world records for the marathon race walks at the All Japan Race Walking meet in Takahata on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan's Masatora Kawano and Australia's Rebecca Henderson set the men's and women's world records for the marathon race walks at the All Japan Race Walking meet in Takahata on Sunday. Kawano, a two-time world championships medallist in the 35-km event, set the inaugural men’s world record for the distance, with a time of 2:55:14. Henderson improved on Italian [USN:L1N44C02R TEXT:"Sofia Fiorini's record"] from the European Athletics Championships, clocking 3:14:52 at the World Athletics Race Walking Tour Bronze event. The half marathon and marathon became official race walk distances in January this year.

item.title: Flames continue turnaround, top Wings for third straight win
item.description: Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as the Calgary Flames cruised past the visiting Detroit Red Wings 4-1 on Saturday, snapping Detroit's eight-game winning streak in the teams' series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as the Calgary Flames cruised past the visiting Detroit Red Wings 4-1 on Saturday, snapping Detroit's eight-game winning streak in the teams' series. Matvei Gridin had a goal and an assist for Calgary, while Ryan Strome and Zayne Parekh also scored. Matt Coronato added two assists. Devin Cooley made 28 saves for the Flames, who have won three straight and four of their last five games after opening the season with five consecutive losses. Andrew Copp scored the lone goal for Detroit, which had won three of its previous four games. John Gibson made 21 saves after leaving his previous start Thursday because of an eye issue. Farabee, who extended his point streak to four games with two goals and four assists during that span, put Calgary on the board at 17:50 of the first period. Adam Klapka set him up for a snap shot, while Kevin Bahl also assisted on Farabee's second goal of the season. Copp tied the game at 2:22 of the second period with his second goal of the season. J.T. Compher set him up for a backhand shot past Cooley. Parekh put Calgary back in front at 8:38 with a power-play snap shot for his first goal of the season. Strome extended the lead to 3-1 at 17:04, converting a pass from Morgan Frost for his second goal of the season. Gridin capped the scoring at 18:30 of the second period with a power-play snap shot for his second goal of the campaign. The Flames will look to complete a sweep of their four-game homestand Monday against the Toronto Maple Leafs, while the Red Wings will try to split their four-game road trip Monday against the Edmonton Oilers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australian Grand Prix called off as rain spoils Phillip Island send-off
item.description: The MotoGP race was delayed by two hours due to the weather, before organisers threw in the towel and finally called it off.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The final Australian MotoGP at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit was called off on Sunday due to heavy rain, ruining the farewell for one of the championship's most beloved circuits. It was a crushing blow for the sold-out crowd [USN:L6N46607H TEXT:"at Phillip Island,"] with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the streets of Adelaide next year. The Moto2 and Moto3 races were cancelled first and the MotoGP race was delayed by two hours due to the weather, before organisers threw in the towel and finally called it off at 3:40 p.m. (0440 GMT). "Due to limited visibility affecting the operation of the medical helicopter the MotoGP Grand Prix race has been cancelled," MotoGP said in a statement. "The MotoGP riders will do a lap behind the safety car and stop on the main straight to greet the fans. Pitlane will open for the farewell lap at 15:45 local time." RIDER PARADE The dark clouds and pelting rain brought down the visibility around the circuit, affecting the medical helicopter, which would take 45 minutes to reach the circuit from mainland Melbourne in an emergency. Other than two years lost to the COVID-19 pandemic, the seaside track south of Melbourne had been a fixture on the world championship calendar for 30 years and produced some of Australian motorcycling's most memorable moments. Australian two-times world champion Casey Stoner celebrated six wins in succession from 2007 to 2012, while compatriot Mick Doohan sealed his fifth and final world title with victory in the 1998 race. The raincoat-clad fans who persevered through the rain were treated to a farewell lap from the MotoGP riders, who waved as they slowly made their way around a soaking wet track. Home racer Jack Miller did his best to entertain his supporters with a series of tricks, including a stand-up wheelie over the finish line, before heading over to the grandstand and throwing his gloves and boots into the crowd. MILLER DEJECTED, SIGH OF RELIEF FOR MARTIN The Pramac Racing rider, a very strong performer in the wet, cut a dejected figure when he was interviewed after completing his lap. "This is a tough pill to swallow," said the 31-year-old, who will be leaving MotoGP at the end of the season after more than a decade to join Pata Maxus Yamaha in the World Superbike Championship. "You know, I was praying for rain all weekend. We got the rain, but obviously we weren't organised enough to get the racing going, so it's a tough one. "You guys deserve better. Honestly, all of you have done a fantastic job turning out for Phillip Island, sitting through traffic, sitting through dog-shit weather, all the rest of it. You guys are amazing. Thank you very much." Rain had been expected for the weekend, but MotoGP did not revive its 2023 strategy for the circuit, when the Grand Prix was moved ahead to Saturday and the sprint scheduled for Sunday. That sprint race three years ago was eventually called off. The cancellation of the race also ended the opportunity for seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez to extend his lead in the championship standings, with his title rival Martin declared unfit to compete in the race after [USN:L1N46A017 TEXT:"fracturing his wrist."] Martin held the championship lead heading into the weekend but finds himself 10 points behind Marquez after failing to finish Saturday's sprint after a gruesome crash. On Sunday, Martin's team Aprilia said he would not travel back to Spain to undergo treatment, however, boosting the 2024 champion's hopes of racing at next week's Malaysian Grand Prix and remaining in the title fight.

item.title: The young and the restless—capitalism’s year of discontent
item.description: The larger message from the streets may be that the balance between market efficiency and social security has shifted too far.
item.dc:creator: Pravesh Sharma
item.content:encoded:
-->

Opinion

The young and the restless—capitalism’s year of discontent

The larger message from the streets may be that the balance between market efficiency and social security has shifted too far.

Pravesh Sharma

25 October, 2026 10:43 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

A demonstrator kicks a tear-gas-emitting object during a student protest in Brussels, Belgium on Saturday | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

S omething unusual is stirring on the streets of the world.

The immediate causes are different. In Bangladesh, a student protest over quotas in public employment grew into something much bigger. In Nepal, restrictions on social media provided the spark, but behind them lay accumulated anger over corruption, economic stagnation, and the conspicuous lifestyles of a privileged political class. Both countries endured extended periods of chaos that resulted in a reset of the political landscape.

India has seen its own manifestations of youth anger, first around entrance examinations and paper leaks, and subsequently about the revision of electoral rolls. Even though the protest e rs in India have remained steadfastly non-violent and do not advocate larger political changes, the government views them with unease. More recently, young people have been prominent in demonstrations, often violent, across France, Belgium, Italy, and Albania.

Show Full Article

There is ostensibly no common organisation linking these movements, no shared manifesto, and certainly no single ideology. Their political circumstances are very different. It would be simplistic to describe them as one global movement. But it would be equally unwise to ignore the common undertow.

Those left behind by the ‘new economy’ Much of the anger stems from a generation beginning to doubt the economic bargain offered to it. For several decades, the legitimacy of market capitalism rested on a relatively simple proposition : Economic growth would create opportunities ; e ducation would enable social mobility ; and h ard work would be rewarded. Each generation could reasonably expect to live somewhat better than the previous one. The state, meanwhile, would provide a reasonable floor of schools, universities, healthcare, transport, and social protection.

That bargain looks increasingly uncertain. Global youth unemployment remains high, with the college-educated cohort disproportionately impacted. But statistics tell only part of the story. Many traditional entry points into secure middle-class employment are shrinking. Young people increasingly encounter temporary work, stagnant incomes, expensive housing, and intense competition for a limited number of secure jobs. They are invited to celebrate the “new economy” and its gig-like character, which many are understandably reluctant to do.

For an educated young person, unemployment is not merely the absence of income. It represents a broken expectation. Families invest heavily in education because they see it as the route to economic mobility. When degrees no longer lead reliably to employment and competitive examinations become lotteries involving millions of applicants, frustration inevitably acquires a political dimension.

This helps explain why education and employment have repeatedly become flashpoints. The youth-led upheaval in Bangladesh began with access to government jobs. The protests in India against paper leaks reflected the enormous stakes attached to a limited number of opportunities. Across parts of Europe, students, teachers, and workers have protested over education funding, wages, and deteriorating public services.

These are d ifferent grievances, certainly, but behind them lurks a single question: what future does society offer its young? This question has become more urgent as economic insecurity coincid es with pressures on the public services on which citizens depend.

Governments everywhere face genuine fiscal constraints. Populations are ageing. Public debt has risen. Healthcare costs are growing. Defence and security expenditure is increasing. In countries such as India, an enormous buildout of economic and social infrastructure is still needed, much of it to be undertaken by the government. These pressures cannot simply be wished away.

Yet, there are political consequences when fiscal adjustment translates into poorer schools, more expensive universities, unaffordable housing, weaker social protection, and increasingly strained healthcare. What appears in a government budget as expenditure rationalisation can seem vastly different to a young citizen struggling to establish an independent life.

Also read: What H&M’s decline and Zara’s growth mean for India’s apparel industry

Time to renew the social contract Parallel to this crisis, another, potentially more unsettling development is taking place: the extraordinary visibility of concentrated wealth. Capitalism has always produced inequality. What has changed is both its scale in some societies and its visibility everywhere. Young people facing insecure employment and uncertain prospects simultaneously inhabit a digital world in which enormous private fortunes and extravagant lifestyles are displayed and lauded continuously. Nepal offers an unusually vivid illustration , where the lifestyles associated with the families of powerful people became a lightning rod for a wider resentment.

But the issue goes beyond conspicuous consumption. Across countries, enormously wealthy individuals and corporations possess growing influence over technology, media, political campaigns, and public debate. Successful enterprise, innovation, and risk-taking remain essential engines of prosperity. Wealth in itself is hardly the problem. The difficulty begins when citizens believe that wealth can purchase disproportionate political influence—or that the rules governing ordinary people do not apply equally to those at the top. Inequality ceases to be a distant economic statistic then, and becomes injustice deeply felt by young people.

A n uncomfortable relationship is emerging between economic discontent and populist politics. In several democracies, sections of the wealthy have found common cause with R ight-wing populist movements promising lower taxes, deregulation, or protection from institutional constraints. Populist leaders have often proved adept at redirecting economic anxiety toward immigration, cultural identity, minorities, or established institutions.

The paradox is striking. Citizens frustrated by economic insecurity can end up supporting political movements whose economic programmes do relatively little to alter the underlying distribution of wealth and opportunity. This is why viewing the current global unrest simply through the familiar prism of ‘ Left versus Right ’ misses something important. Many young protesters do not speak the language of traditional ideology. They speak about jobs, examinations, rent, schools, corruption, dignity, and fairness. They organise through social media rather than political parties or trade unions. Their mobilisation can therefore be sudden, decentralised, and unpredictable.

The fact remains that every street protest can’t be romanticised. Protest movements can appear to be incoherent. Legitimate demonstrations can descend into violence. Social media can amplify misinformation as readily as genuine grievances. Governments have a mandate and responsibility to maintain public order. But maintaining order and understanding discontent are different tasks.

The larger message from the streets may be that the balance between market efficiency and social security has shifted too far. Capitalism has demonstrated an extraordinary ability to generate wealth, innovation, and technological progress. But its political legitimacy ultimately depends on something more: enough people must believe that they have a reasonable opportunity to participate in that prosperity.

The social contract everywhere is in urgent need of renewal. That means restoring opportunity and social mobility; protecting reasonable access to education, healthcare, and housing; ensuring genuine competition rather than entrenched economic power; and maintaining credible boundaries between wealth and political influence. Governments worldwide must recognise that economic growth, while indispensable, cannot be the only measure of a successful society.

Pravesh Sharma is a former IAS officer who served in Madhya Pradesh, the PMO, and the UN. Views are personal.

(Edited by Prasanna Bachchhav)

item.title: Devin Booker, Suns continue Warriors' rough start to season
item.description: Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds and the host Phoenix Suns beat Golden State 131-122 on Saturday to send the Warriors to their worst start in almost two decades.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds and the host Phoenix Suns beat Golden State 131-122 on Saturday to send the Warriors to their worst start in almost two decades. Miles Bridges scored 16 points and Dillon Brooks added 15 points for the Suns, who won their home opener after suffering a 41-point defeat at Portland in their season opener Wednesday. Booker set a franchise record for points in a home opener. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 26 points and nine rebounds and De'Anthony Melton scored 20 of his 25 points in the second half for the skeleton-crew Warriors, who fell to 0-3 for the first time since 2007-08, when they lost their first six before finishing 48-34. Golden State, playing the second of a back-to-back, was without starters Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski and Draymond Green and reserve Al Horford. Curry (knee), Podziemski (back) and Horford (back) were held out for injury management. Green missed with low back soreness. Brandon Williams added 20 points for the Warriors, who blew a 12-point lead in the final four minutes of a 111-108 home loss to Memphis on Friday. Lendeborg made six of the Warriors' 17 3-pointers on Saturday. Melton had four. Melton scored 13 points in the third quarter, when the Warriors used a 12-0 run to take a 73-71 lead before the Suns came back. Booker's four-point play with 35 seconds left in the third quarter made it 99-89 for Phoenix. Luke Kennard's 3-pointer pushed the Suns' lead to 117-102 with 6:07 remaining in the game. Kennard had 11 points and three 3-pointers in his Suns debut after missing the season opener with a knee injury. The Warriors made 17 of 39 3-pointers (43.6%) and turned 19 offensive rebounds into 26 points. The Suns knocked the Warriors out of the postseason a year ago with a 111-96 victory in the play-in round. Lendeborg had six points on a pair of threes and Graham Ike had six points and five rebounds in the first quarter, when the Warriors took an early seven-point lead and had a 25-22 edge at the quarter. Ike, a 6-foot-9 rookie, made his second straight start at center as the Warriors also played without Kristaps Porzingis, who is not with the team because of an undisclosed health issue. --Field Level Media
